232     def process(app: Sphinx, what_: str, name: str, obj: Any, options: Any, lines: List[str]
233                 ) -> None:
234         if what and what_ not in what:
235             return
236         deleted = 0
237         delete = not exclude
238         orig_lines = lines[:]
239         for i, line in enumerate(orig_lines):
240             if delete:
241                 lines.pop(i - deleted)
242                 deleted += 1
243             if marker_re.match(line):
244                 delete = not delete
245                 if delete:
246                     lines.pop(i - deleted)
247                     deleted += 1
248         if not lines and not keepempty:
249             lines[:] = orig_lines
250         # make sure there is a blank line at the end
251         if lines and lines[-1]:
252             lines.append('')

641     def get_object_members(self, want_all: bool) -> Tuple[bool, ObjectMembers]:
642         """Return `(members_check_module, members)` where `members` is a
643         list of `(membername, member)` pairs of the members of *self.object*.
644

646         members given by *self.options.members* (which may also be none).

649                       'removed from Sphinx-6.0.', RemovedInSphinx60Warning)
650         members = get_object_members(self.object, self.objpath, self.get_attr, self.analyzer)
651         if not want_all:
652             if not self.options.members:
653                 return False, []  # type: ignore
654             # specific members given
655             selected = []
656             for name in self.options.members:  # type: str
657                 if name in members:
658                     selected.append((name, members[name].value))
659                 else:
660                     logger.warning(__('missing attribute %s in object %s') %
661                                    (name, self.fullname), type='autodoc')
662             return False, selected

669     def filter_members(self, members: ObjectMembers, want_all: bool
670                        ) -> List[Tuple[str, Any, bool]]:
671         """Filter the given member list.
672 
673         Members are skipped if
674 
675         - they are private (except if given explicitly or the private-members
676           option is set)
677         - they are special methods (except if given explicitly or the
678           special-members option is set)
679         - they are undocumented (except if the undoc-members option is set)
680 
681         The user can override the skipping decision by connecting to the
682         ``autodoc-skip-member`` event.
683         """
684         def is_filtered_inherited_member(name: str, obj: Any) -> bool:
685             if inspect.isclass(self.object):
686                 for cls in self.object.__mro__:
687                     if cls.__name__ == self.options.inherited_members and cls != self.object:
688                         # given member is a member of specified *super class*
689                         return True
690                     elif name in cls.__dict__:
691                         return False
692                     elif name in self.get_attr(cls, '__annotations__', {}):
693                         return False
694                     elif isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.class_ is cls:
695                         return False
696 
697             return False
698 
699         ret = []
700 
701         # search for members in source code too
702         namespace = '.'.join(self.objpath)  # will be empty for modules
703 
704         if self.analyzer:
705             attr_docs = self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
706         else:
707             attr_docs = {}
708 
709         # process members and determine which to skip
710         for obj in members:
711             membername, member = obj
712             # if isattr is True, the member is documented as an attribute
713             if member is INSTANCEATTR:
714                 isattr = True
715             elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
716                 isattr = True
717             else:
718                 isattr = False
719 
720             doc = getdoc(member, self.get_attr, self.config.autodoc_inherit_docstrings,
721                          self.parent, self.object_name)
722             if not isinstance(doc, str):
723                 # Ignore non-string __doc__
724                 doc = None
725 
726             # if the member __doc__ is the same as self's __doc__, it's just
727             # inherited and therefore not the member's doc
728             cls = self.get_attr(member, '__class__', None)
729             if cls:
730                 cls_doc = self.get_attr(cls, '__doc__', None)
731                 if cls_doc == doc:
732                     doc = None
733 
734             if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.docstring:
735                 # hack for ClassDocumenter to inject docstring via ObjectMember
736                 doc = obj.docstring
737 
738             doc, metadata = separate_metadata(doc)
739             has_doc = bool(doc)
740 
741             if 'private' in metadata:
742                 # consider a member private if docstring has "private" metadata
743                 isprivate = True
744             elif 'public' in metadata:
745                 # consider a member public if docstring has "public" metadata
746                 isprivate = False
747             else:
748                 isprivate = membername.startswith('_')
749 
750             keep = False
751             if ismock(member):
752                 # mocked module or object
753                 pass
754             elif self.options.exclude_members and membername in self.options.exclude_members:
755                 # remove members given by exclude-members
756                 keep = False
757             elif want_all and special_member_re.match(membername):
758                 # special __methods__
759                 if self.options.special_members and membername in self.options.special_members:
760                     if membername == '__doc__':
761                         keep = False
762                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
763                         keep = False
764                     else:
765                         keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
766                 else:
767                     keep = False
768             elif (namespace, membername) in attr_docs:
769                 if want_all and isprivate:
770                     if self.options.private_members is None:
771                         keep = False
772                     else:
773                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
774                 else:
775                     # keep documented attributes
776                     keep = True
777             elif want_all and isprivate:
778                 if has_doc or self.options.undoc_members:
779                     if self.options.private_members is None:
780                         keep = False
781                     elif is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj):
782                         keep = False
783                     else:
784                         keep = membername in self.options.private_members
785                 else:
786                     keep = False
787             else:
788                 if (self.options.members is ALL and
789                         is_filtered_inherited_member(membername, obj)):
790                     keep = False
791                 else:
792                     # ignore undocumented members if :undoc-members: is not given
793                     keep = has_doc or self.options.undoc_members
794 
795             if isinstance(obj, ObjectMember) and obj.skipped:
796                 # forcedly skipped member (ex. a module attribute not defined in __all__)
797                 keep = False
798 
799             # give the user a chance to decide whether this member
800             # should be skipped
801             if self.env.app:
802                 # let extensions preprocess docstrings
803                 try:
804                     skip_user = self.env.app.emit_firstresult(
805                         'autodoc-skip-member', self.objtype, membername, member,
806                         not keep, self.options)
807                     if skip_user is not None:
808                         keep = not skip_user
809                 except Exception as exc:
810                     logger.warning(__('autodoc: failed to determine %r to be documented, '
811                                       'the following exception was raised:\n%s'),
812                                    member, exc, type='autodoc')
813                     keep = False
814 
815             if keep:
816                 ret.append((membername, member, isattr))
817 
818         return ret

820     def document_members(self, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
821         """Generate reST for member documentation.
822 
823         If *all_members* is True, do all members, else those given by
824         *self.options.members*.
825         """
826         # set current namespace for finding members
827         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = self.modname
828         if self.objpath:
829             self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = self.objpath[0]
830 
831         want_all = (all_members or
832                     self.options.inherited_members or
833                     self.options.members is ALL)
834         # find out which members are documentable
835         members_check_module, members = self.get_object_members(want_all)
836 
837         # document non-skipped members
838         memberdocumenters: List[Tuple[Documenter, bool]] = []
839         for (mname, member, isattr) in self.filter_members(members, want_all):
840             classes = [cls for cls in self.documenters.values()
841                        if cls.can_document_member(member, mname, isattr, self)]
842             if not classes:
843                 # don't know how to document this member
844                 continue
845             # prefer the documenter with the highest priority
846             classes.sort(key=lambda cls: cls.priority)
847             # give explicitly separated module name, so that members
848             # of inner classes can be documented
849             full_mname = self.modname + '::' + '.'.join(self.objpath + [mname])
850             documenter = classes[-1](self.directive, full_mname, self.indent)
851             memberdocumenters.append((documenter, isattr))
852 
853         member_order = self.options.member_order or self.config.autodoc_member_order
854         memberdocumenters = self.sort_members(memberdocumenters, member_order)
855 
856         for documenter, isattr in memberdocumenters:
857             documenter.generate(
858                 all_members=True, real_modname=self.real_modname,
859                 check_module=members_check_module and not isattr)
860 
861         # reset current objects
862         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:module'] = None
863         self.env.temp_data['autodoc:class'] = None
864 
865     def sort_members(self, documenters: List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]],
866                      order: str) -> List[Tuple["Documenter", bool]]:
867         """Sort the given member list."""
868         if order == 'groupwise':
869             # sort by group; alphabetically within groups
870             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: (e[0].member_order, e[0].name))
871         elif order == 'bysource':
872             if self.analyzer:
873                 # sort by source order, by virtue of the module analyzer
874                 tagorder = self.analyzer.tagorder
875 
876                 def keyfunc(entry: Tuple[Documenter, bool]) -> int:
877                     fullname = entry[0].name.split('::')[1]
878                     return tagorder.get(fullname, len(tagorder))
879                 documenters.sort(key=keyfunc)
880             else:
881                 # Assume that member discovery order matches source order.
882                 # This is a reasonable assumption in Python 3.6 and up, where
883                 # module.__dict__ is insertion-ordered.
884                 pass
885         else:  # alphabetical
886             documenters.sort(key=lambda e: e[0].name)
887 
888         return documenters
889 
890     def generate(self, more_content: Optional[StringList] = None, real_modname: str = None,
891                  check_module: bool = False, all_members: bool = False) -> None:
892         """Generate reST for the object given by *self.name*, and possibly for
893         its members.
894 
895         If *more_content* is given, include that content. If *real_modname* is
896         given, use that module name to find attribute docs. If *check_module* is
897         True, only generate if the object is defined in the module name it is
898         imported from. If *all_members* is True, document all members.
899         """
900         if not self.parse_name():
901             # need a module to import
902             logger.warning(
903                 __('don\'t know which module to import for autodocumenting '
904                    '%r (try placing a "module" or "currentmodule" directive '
905                    'in the document, or giving an explicit module name)') %
906                 self.name, type='autodoc')
907             return
908 
909         # now, import the module and get object to document
910         if not self.import_object():
911             return
912 
913         # If there is no real module defined, figure out which to use.
914         # The real module is used in the module analyzer to look up the module
915         # where the attribute documentation would actually be found in.
916         # This is used for situations where you have a module that collects the
917         # functions and classes of internal submodules.
918         guess_modname = self.get_real_modname()
919         self.real_modname: str = real_modname or guess_modname
920 
921         # try to also get a source code analyzer for attribute docs
922         try:
923             self.analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(self.real_modname)
924             # parse right now, to get PycodeErrors on parsing (results will
925             # be cached anyway)
926             self.analyzer.find_attr_docs()
927         except PycodeError as exc:
928             logger.debug('[autodoc] module analyzer failed: %s', exc)
929             # no source file -- e.g. for builtin and C modules
930             self.analyzer = None
931             # at least add the module.__file__ as a dependency
932             if hasattr(self.module, '__file__') and self.module.__file__:
933                 self.directive.record_dependencies.add(self.module.__file__)
934         else:
935             self.directive.record_dependencies.add(self.analyzer.srcname)
936 
937         if self.real_modname != guess_modname:
938             # Add module to dependency list if target object is defined in other module.
939             try:
940                 analyzer = ModuleAnalyzer.for_module(guess_modname)
941                 self.directive.record_dependencies.add(analyzer.srcname)
942             except PycodeError:
943                 pass
944 
945         # check __module__ of object (for members not given explicitly)
946         if check_module:
947             if not self.check_module():
948                 return
949 
950         sourcename = self.get_sourcename()
951 
952         # make sure that the result starts with an empty line.  This is
953         # necessary for some situations where another directive preprocesses
954         # reST and no starting newline is present
955         self.add_line('', sourcename)
956 
957         # format the object's signature, if any
958         try:
959             sig = self.format_signature()
960         except Exception as exc:
961             logger.warning(__('error while formatting signature for %s: %s'),
962                            self.fullname, exc, type='autodoc')
963             return
964 
965         # generate the directive header and options, if applicable
966         self.add_directive_header(sig)
967         self.add_line('', sourcename)
968 
969         # e.g. the module directive doesn't have content
970         self.indent += self.content_indent
971 
972         # add all content (from docstrings, attribute docs etc.)
973         self.add_content(more_content)
974 
975         # document members, if possible
976         self.document_members(all_members)
977

1177 class DocstringSignatureMixin:
1178     """
1179     Mixin for FunctionDocumenter and MethodDocumenter to provide the
1180     feature of reading the signature from the docstring.
1181     """
1182     _new_docstrings: List[List[str]] = None
1183     _signatures: List[str] = None
1184 
1185     def _find_signature(self) -> Tuple[str, str]:
1186         # candidates of the object name
1187         valid_names = [self.objpath[-1]]  # type: ignore
1188         if isinstance(self, ClassDocumenter):
1189             valid_names.append('__init__')
1190             if hasattr(self.object, '__mro__'):
1191                 valid_names.extend(cls.__name__ for cls in self.object.__mro__)
1192 
1193         docstrings = self.get_doc()
1194         if docstrings is None:
1195             return None, None
1196         self._new_docstrings = docstrings[:]
1197         self._signatures = []
1198         result = None
1199         for i, doclines in enumerate(docstrings):
1200             for j, line in enumerate(doclines):
1201                 if not line:
1202                     # no lines in docstring, no match
1203                     break
1204 
1205                 if line.endswith('\\'):
1206                     line = line.rstrip('\\').rstrip()
1207 
1208                 # match first line of docstring against signature RE
1209                 match = py_ext_sig_re.match(line)
1210                 if not match:
1211                     break
1212                 exmod, path, base, args, retann = match.groups()
1213 
1214                 # the base name must match ours
1215                 if base not in valid_names:
1216                     break
1217 
1218                 # re-prepare docstring to ignore more leading indentation
1219                 tab_width = self.directive.state.document.settings.tab_width  # type: ignore
1220                 self._new_docstrings[i] = prepare_docstring('\n'.join(doclines[j + 1:]),
1221                                                             tabsize=tab_width)
1222 
1223                 if result is None:
1224                     # first signature
1225                     result = args, retann
1226                 else:
1227                     # subsequent signatures
1228                     self._signatures.append("(%s) -> %s" % (args, retann))
1229 
1230             if result:
1231                 # finish the loop when signature found
1232                 break
1233 
1234         return result
1235 
1236     def get_doc(self, ignore: int = None) -> List[List[str]]:
1237         if self._new_docstrings is not None:
1238             return self._new_docstrings
1239         return super().get_doc(ignore)  # type: ignore
1240 
1241     def format_signature(self, **kwargs: Any) -> str:
1242         if self.args is None and self.config.autodoc_docstring_signature:  # type: ignore
1243             # only act if a signature is not explicitly given already, and if
1244             # the feature is enabled
1245             result = self._find_signature()
1246             if result is not None:
1247                 self.args, self.retann = result
1248         sig = super().format_signature(**kwargs)  # type: ignore
1249         if self._signatures:
1250             return "\n".join([sig] + self._signatures)
1251         else:
1252             return sig

1473     def _get_signature(self) -> Tuple[Optional[Any], Optional[str], Optional[Signature]]:
1474         def get_user_defined_function_or_method(obj: Any, attr: str) -> Any:
1475             """ Get the `attr` function or method from `obj`, if it is user-defined. """
1476             if inspect.is_builtin_class_method(obj, attr):
1477                 return None
1478             attr = self.get_attr(obj, attr, None)
1479             if not (inspect.ismethod(attr) or inspect.isfunction(attr)):
1480                 return None

1483         # This sequence is copied from inspect._signature_from_callable.
1484         # ValueError means that no signature could be found, so we keep going.
1485 
1486         # First, we check the obj has a __signature__ attribute
1487         if (hasattr(self.object, '__signature__') and
1488                 isinstance(self.object.__signature__, Signature)):
1489             return None, None, self.object.__signature__
1490 
1491         # Next, let's see if it has an overloaded __call__ defined
1492         # in its metaclass
1493         call = get_user_defined_function_or_method(type(self.object), '__call__')
1494 
1495         if call is not None:
1496             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(call) in _METACLASS_CALL_BLACKLIST:
1497                 call = None
1498

1500             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', call, True)
1501             try:
1502                 sig = inspect.signature(call, bound_method=True,
1503                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1504                 return type(self.object), '__call__', sig
1505             except ValueError:
1506                 pass
1507 
1508         # Now we check if the 'obj' class has a '__new__' method
1509         new = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__new__')
1510 
1511         if new is not None:
1512             if "{0.__module__}.{0.__qualname__}".format(new) in _CLASS_NEW_BLACKLIST:
1513                 new = None
1514 
1515         if new is not None:
1516             self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', new, True)
1517             try:
1518                 sig = inspect.signature(new, bound_method=True,
1519                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1520                 return self.object, '__new__', sig
1521             except ValueError:
1522                 pass

1525         init = get_user_defined_function_or_method(self.object, '__init__')

1530                                         type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)

1533                 pass

1538         # the signature from, so just pass the object itself to our hook.
1539         self.env.app.emit('autodoc-before-process-signature', self.object, False)

1542                                     type_aliases=self.config.autodoc_type_aliases)
1543             return None, None, sig
1544         except ValueError:
1545             pass
1546

1548         # with __init__ in C and no `__text_signature__`.

433 def object_description(object: Any) -> str:
434     """A repr() implementation that returns text safe to use in reST context."""
435     if isinstance(object, dict):
436         try:
437             sorted_keys = sorted(object)
438         except Exception:
439             pass  # Cannot sort dict keys, fall back to generic repr
440         else:
441             items = ("%s: %s" %
442                      (object_description(key), object_description(object[key]))
443                      for key in sorted_keys)
444             return "{%s}" % ", ".join(items)
445     elif isinstance(object, set):
446         try:
447             sorted_values = sorted(object)
448         except TypeError:
449             pass  # Cannot sort set values, fall back to generic repr
450         else:
451             return "{%s}" % ", ".join(object_description(x) for x in sorted_values)
452     elif isinstance(object, frozenset):
453         try:
454             sorted_values = sorted(object)
455         except TypeError:
456             pass  # Cannot sort frozenset values, fall back to generic repr
457         else:
458             return "frozenset({%s})" % ", ".join(object_description(x)
459                                                  for x in sorted_values)
460     elif isinstance(object, enum.Enum):
461         return "%s.%s" % (object.__class__.__name__, object.name)
462 
463     try:
464         s = repr(object)
465     except Exception as exc:
466         raise ValueError from exc
467     # Strip non-deterministic memory addresses such as
468     # ``<__main__.A at 0x7f68cb685710>``
469     s = memory_address_re.sub('', s)
470     return s.replace('\n', ' ')

592 def signature(subject: Callable, bound_method: bool = False, follow_wrapped: bool = None,
593               type_aliases: Dict = {}) -> inspect.Signature:
594     """Return a Signature object for the given *subject*.
595 
596     :param bound_method: Specify *subject* is a bound method or not
597     :param follow_wrapped: Same as ``inspect.signature()``.
598     """
599 
600     if follow_wrapped is None:
601         follow_wrapped = True
602     else:
603         warnings.warn('The follow_wrapped argument of sphinx.util.inspect.signature() is '
604                       'deprecated', RemovedInSphinx50Warning, stacklevel=2)
605 
606     try:
607         try:
608             if _should_unwrap(subject):
609                 signature = inspect.signature(subject)
610             else:
611                 signature = inspect.signature(subject, follow_wrapped=follow_wrapped)
612         except ValueError:
613             # follow built-in wrappers up (ex. functools.lru_cache)
614             signature = inspect.signature(subject)
615         parameters = list(signature.parameters.values())
616         return_annotation = signature.return_annotation
617     except IndexError:
618         # Until python 3.6.4, cpython has been crashed on inspection for
619         # partialmethods not having any arguments.
620         # https://bugs.python.org/issue33009
621         if hasattr(subject, '_partialmethod'):
622             parameters = []
623             return_annotation = Parameter.empty
624         else:
625             raise
626 
627     try:
628         # Resolve annotations using ``get_type_hints()`` and type_aliases.
629         localns = TypeAliasNamespace(type_aliases)
630         annotations = typing.get_type_hints(subject, None, localns)
631         for i, param in enumerate(parameters):
632             if param.name in annotations:
633                 annotation = annotations[param.name]
634                 if isinstance(annotation, TypeAliasForwardRef):
635                     annotation = annotation.name
636                 parameters[i] = param.replace(annotation=annotation)
637         if 'return' in annotations:
638             if isinstance(annotations['return'], TypeAliasForwardRef):
639                 return_annotation = annotations['return'].name
640             else:
641                 return_annotation = annotations['return']
642     except Exception:
643         # ``get_type_hints()`` does not support some kind of objects like partial,
644         # ForwardRef and so on.
645         pass
646 
647     if bound_method:
648         if inspect.ismethod(subject):
649             # ``inspect.signature()`` considers the subject is a bound method and removes
650             # first argument from signature.  Therefore no skips are needed here.
651             pass
652         else:
653             if len(parameters) > 0:
654                 parameters.pop(0)
655 
656     # To allow to create signature object correctly for pure python functions,
657     # pass an internal parameter __validate_parameters__=False to Signature
658     #
659     # For example, this helps a function having a default value `inspect._empty`.
660     # refs: https://github.com/sphinx-doc/sphinx/issues/7935
661     return inspect.Signature(parameters, return_annotation=return_annotation,  # type: ignore
662                              __validate_parameters__=False)

665 def evaluate_signature(sig: inspect.Signature, globalns: Dict = None, localns: Dict = None
666                        ) -> inspect.Signature:
667     """Evaluate unresolved type annotations in a signature object."""
668     def evaluate_forwardref(ref: ForwardRef, globalns: Dict, localns: Dict) -> Any:
669         """Evaluate a forward reference."""
670         if sys.version_info > (3, 9):
671             return ref._evaluate(globalns, localns, frozenset())
672         else:
673             return ref._evaluate(globalns, localns)
674 
675     def evaluate(annotation: Any, globalns: Dict, localns: Dict) -> Any:
676         """Evaluate unresolved type annotation."""
677         try:
678             if isinstance(annotation, str):
679                 ref = ForwardRef(annotation, True)
680                 annotation = evaluate_forwardref(ref, globalns, localns)
681 
682                 if isinstance(annotation, ForwardRef):
683                     annotation = evaluate_forwardref(ref, globalns, localns)
684                 elif isinstance(annotation, str):
685                     # might be a ForwardRef'ed annotation in overloaded functions
686                     ref = ForwardRef(annotation, True)
687                     annotation = evaluate_forwardref(ref, globalns, localns)
688         except (NameError, TypeError):
689             # failed to evaluate type. skipped.
690             pass
691 
692         return annotation
693 
694     if globalns is None:
695         globalns = {}
696     if localns is None:
697         localns = globalns
698 
699     parameters = list(sig.parameters.values())
700     for i, param in enumerate(parameters):
701         if param.annotation:
702             annotation = evaluate(param.annotation, globalns, localns)
703             parameters[i] = param.replace(annotation=annotation)
704 
705     return_annotation = sig.return_annotation
706     if return_annotation:
707         return_annotation = evaluate(return_annotation, globalns, localns)
708 
709     return sig.replace(parameters=parameters, return_annotation=return_annotation)

712 def stringify_signature(sig: inspect.Signature, show_annotation: bool = True,
713                         show_return_annotation: bool = True) -> str:
714     """Stringify a Signature object.
715 
716     :param show_annotation: Show annotation in result
717     """
718     args = []
719     last_kind = None
720     for param in sig.parameters.values():
721         if param.kind != param.POSITIONAL_ONLY and last_kind == param.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
722             # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
723             args.append('/')
724         if param.kind == param.KEYWORD_ONLY and last_kind in (param.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
725                                                               param.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
726                                                               None):
727             # PEP-3102: Separator for Keyword Only Parameter: *
728             args.append('*')
729 
730         arg = StringIO()
731         if param.kind == param.VAR_POSITIONAL:
732             arg.write('*' + param.name)
733         elif param.kind == param.VAR_KEYWORD:
734             arg.write('**' + param.name)
735         else:
736             arg.write(param.name)
737 
738         if show_annotation and param.annotation is not param.empty:
739             arg.write(': ')
740             arg.write(stringify_annotation(param.annotation))
741         if param.default is not param.empty:
742             if show_annotation and param.annotation is not param.empty:
743                 arg.write(' = ')
744             else:
745                 arg.write('=')
746             arg.write(object_description(param.default))
747 
748         args.append(arg.getvalue())
749         last_kind = param.kind
750 
751     if last_kind == Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY:
752         # PEP-570: Separator for Positional Only Parameter: /
753         args.append('/')
754 
755     if (sig.return_annotation is Parameter.empty or
756             show_annotation is False or
757             show_return_annotation is False):
758         return '(%s)' % ', '.join(args)
759     else:
760         annotation = stringify_annotation(sig.return_annotation)
761         return '(%s) -> %s' % (', '.join(args), annotation)

773 def signature_from_ast(node: ast.FunctionDef, code: str = '') -> inspect.Signature:
774     """Create a Signature object from AST *node*."""
775     args = node.args
776     defaults = list(args.defaults)
777     params = []
778     if hasattr(args, "posonlyargs"):
779         posonlyargs = len(args.posonlyargs)  # type: ignore
780         positionals = posonlyargs + len(args.args)
781     else:
782         posonlyargs = 0
783         positionals = len(args.args)
784 
785     for _ in range(len(defaults), positionals):
786         defaults.insert(0, Parameter.empty)
787 
788     if hasattr(args, "posonlyargs"):
789         for i, arg in enumerate(args.posonlyargs):  # type: ignore
790             if defaults[i] is Parameter.empty:
791                 default = Parameter.empty
792             else:
793                 default = DefaultValue(ast_unparse(defaults[i], code))
794 
795             annotation = ast_unparse(arg.annotation, code) or Parameter.empty
796             params.append(Parameter(arg.arg, Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
797                                     default=default, annotation=annotation))
798 
799     for i, arg in enumerate(args.args):
800         if defaults[i + posonlyargs] is Parameter.empty:
801             default = Parameter.empty
802         else:
803             default = DefaultValue(ast_unparse(defaults[i + posonlyargs], code))
804 
805         annotation = ast_unparse(arg.annotation, code) or Parameter.empty
806         params.append(Parameter(arg.arg, Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
807                                 default=default, annotation=annotation))
808 
809     if args.vararg:
810         annotation = ast_unparse(args.vararg.annotation, code) or Parameter.empty
811         params.append(Parameter(args.vararg.arg, Parameter.VAR_POSITIONAL,
812                                 annotation=annotation))
813 
814     for i, arg in enumerate(args.kwonlyargs):
815         default = ast_unparse(args.kw_defaults[i], code) or Parameter.empty
816         annotation = ast_unparse(arg.annotation, code) or Parameter.empty
817         params.append(Parameter(arg.arg, Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY, default=default,
818                                 annotation=annotation))
819 
820     if args.kwarg:
821         annotation = ast_unparse(args.kwarg.annotation, code) or Parameter.empty
822         params.append(Parameter(args.kwarg.arg, Parameter.VAR_KEYWORD,
823                                 annotation=annotation))
824 
825     return_annotation = ast_unparse(node.returns, code) or Parameter.empty
826 
827     return inspect.Signature(params, return_annotation=return_annotation)

205     def legend(self, *args, **kwargs):
206         """
207         Place a legend on the Axes.
208 
209         Call signatures::
210 
211             legend()
212             legend(handles, labels)
213             legend(handles=handles)
214             legend(labels)

216         The call signatures correspond to the following different ways to use
217         this method:
218 
219         **1. Automatic detection of elements to be shown in the legend**
220 
221         The elements to be added to the legend are automatically determined,
222         when you do not pass in any extra arguments.
223 
224         In this case, the labels are taken from the artist. You can specify
225         them either at artist creation or by calling the
226         :meth:`~.Artist.set_label` method on the artist::
227 
228             ax.plot([1, 2, 3], label='Inline label')
229             ax.legend()
230 
231         or::
232 
233             line, = ax.plot([1, 2, 3])
234             line.set_label('Label via method')
235             ax.legend()
236

238             Specific artists can be excluded from the automatic legend element
239             selection by using a label starting with an underscore, "_".
240             A string starting with an underscore is the default label for all
241             artists, so calling `.Axes.legend` without any arguments and
242             without setting the labels manually will result in no legend being
243             drawn.
244 
245 
246         **2. Explicitly listing the artists and labels in the legend**
247 
248         For full control of which artists have a legend entry, it is possible
249         to pass an iterable of legend artists followed by an iterable of
250         legend labels respectively::
251 
252             ax.legend([line1, line2, line3], ['label1', 'label2', 'label3'])

254

256

258         label properties. Example::
259 
260             line1, = ax.plot([1, 2, 3], label='label1')
261             line2, = ax.plot([1, 2, 3], label='label2')
262             ax.legend(handles=[line1, line2])
263 
264 
265         **4. Labeling existing plot elements**
266 
267         .. admonition:: Discouraged
268 
269             This call signature is discouraged, because the relation between
270             plot elements and labels is only implicit by their order and can
271             easily be mixed up.
272 
273         To make a legend for all artists on an Axes, call this function with
274         an iterable of strings, one for each legend item. For example::
275 
276             ax.plot([1, 2, 3])
277             ax.plot([5, 6, 7])
278             ax.legend(['First line', 'Second line'])
279 
280

282         ----------
283         handles : sequence of `.Artist`, optional
284             A list of Artists (lines, patches) to be added to the legend.
285             Use this together with *labels*, if you need full control on what
286             is shown in the legend and the automatic mechanism described above

289             The length of handles and labels should be the same in this
290             case. If they are not, they are truncated to the smaller length.
291 
292         labels : list of str, optional

407     def indicate_inset(self, bounds, inset_ax=None, *, transform=None,
408                        facecolor='none', edgecolor='0.5', alpha=0.5,
409                        zorder=4.99, **kwargs):
410         """
411         Add an inset indicator to the Axes.  This is a rectangle on the plot
412         at the position indicated by *bounds* that optionally has lines that
413         connect the rectangle to an inset Axes (`.Axes.inset_axes`).
414 
415         Warnings
416         --------
417         This method is experimental as of 3.0, and the API may change.
418 
419         Parameters
420         ----------
421         bounds : [x0, y0, width, height]
422             Lower-left corner of rectangle to be marked, and its width
423             and height.
424 
425         inset_ax : `.Axes`
426             An optional inset Axes to draw connecting lines to.  Two lines are
427             drawn connecting the indicator box to the inset Axes on corners
428             chosen so as to not overlap with the indicator box.
429 
430         transform : `.Transform`
431             Transform for the rectangle coordinates. Defaults to
432             `ax.transAxes`, i.e. the units of *rect* are in Axes-relative
433             coordinates.
434 
435         facecolor : color, default: 'none'
436             Facecolor of the rectangle.
437 
438         edgecolor : color, default: '0.5'
439             Color of the rectangle and color of the connecting lines.
440 
441         alpha : float, default: 0.5
442             Transparency of the rectangle and connector lines.
443 
444         zorder : float, default: 4.99
445             Drawing order of the rectangle and connector lines.  The default,
446             4.99, is just below the default level of inset Axes.
447 
448         **kwargs
449             Other keyword arguments are passed on to the `.Rectangle` patch:
450 
451             %(Rectangle:kwdoc)s
452 
453         Returns
454         -------
455         rectangle_patch : `.patches.Rectangle`
456              The indicator frame.
457 
458         connector_lines : 4-tuple of `.patches.ConnectionPatch`
459             The four connector lines connecting to (lower_left, upper_left,
460             lower_right upper_right) corners of *inset_ax*. Two lines are
461             set with visibility to *False*,  but the user can set the
462             visibility to True if the automatic choice is not deemed correct.
463 
464         """
465         # to make the axes connectors work, we need to apply the aspect to
466         # the parent axes.
467         self.apply_aspect()
468 
469         if transform is None:
470             transform = self.transData
471         kwargs.setdefault('label', '_indicate_inset')
472 
473         x, y, width, height = bounds
474         rectangle_patch = mpatches.Rectangle(
475             (x, y), width, height,
476             facecolor=facecolor, edgecolor=edgecolor, alpha=alpha,
477             zorder=zorder, transform=transform, **kwargs)
478         self.add_patch(rectangle_patch)
479 
480         connects = []
481 
482         if inset_ax is not None:
483             # connect the inset_axes to the rectangle
484             for xy_inset_ax in [(0, 0), (0, 1), (1, 0), (1, 1)]:
485                 # inset_ax positions are in axes coordinates
486                 # The 0, 1 values define the four edges if the inset_ax
487                 # lower_left, upper_left, lower_right upper_right.
488                 ex, ey = xy_inset_ax
489                 if self.xaxis.get_inverted():
490                     ex = 1 - ex
491                 if self.yaxis.get_inverted():
492                     ey = 1 - ey
493                 xy_data = x + ex * width, y + ey * height
494                 p = mpatches.ConnectionPatch(
495                     xyA=xy_inset_ax, coordsA=inset_ax.transAxes,
496                     xyB=xy_data, coordsB=self.transData,
497                     arrowstyle="-", zorder=zorder,
498                     edgecolor=edgecolor, alpha=alpha)
499                 connects.append(p)
500                 self.add_patch(p)
501 
502             # decide which two of the lines to keep visible....
503             pos = inset_ax.get_position()
504             bboxins = pos.transformed(self.figure.transSubfigure)
505             rectbbox = mtransforms.Bbox.from_bounds(
506                 *bounds
507             ).transformed(transform)
508             x0 = rectbbox.x0 < bboxins.x0
509             x1 = rectbbox.x1 < bboxins.x1
510             y0 = rectbbox.y0 < bboxins.y0
511             y1 = rectbbox.y1 < bboxins.y1
512             connects[0].set_visible(x0 ^ y0)
513             connects[1].set_visible(x0 == y1)
514             connects[2].set_visible(x1 == y0)
515             connects[3].set_visible(x1 ^ y1)
516 
517         return rectangle_patch, tuple(connects) if connects else None

1298             (opaque).

1301             the length of *positions*.

1304             Default is 'solid'. Valid strings are ['solid', 'dashed',
1305             'dashdot', 'dotted', '-', '--', '-.', ':']. Dash tuples
1306             should be of the form::

1308                 (offset, onoffseq),
1309 
1310             where *onoffseq* is an even length tuple of on and off ink
1311             in points.

1317             DATA_PARAMETER_PLACEHOLDER

1330         For *linelengths*, *linewidths*, *colors*, *alpha* and *linestyles*, if
1331         only a single value is given, that value is applied to all lines. If an

1363             lineoffsets = [lineoffsets]

1365             linelengths = [linelengths]
1366         if not np.iterable(linewidths):
1367             linewidths = [linewidths]

1369             colors = [colors]

1371             alpha = [alpha]
1372         if hasattr(linestyles, 'lower') or not np.iterable(linestyles):
1373             linestyles = [linestyles]
1374

1377         linewidths = np.asarray(linewidths)
1378

1380             raise ValueError('lineoffsets cannot be empty')
1381         if len(linelengths) == 0:
1382             raise ValueError('linelengths cannot be empty')
1383         if len(linestyles) == 0:

1386             raise ValueError('linewidths cannot be empty')

1406             linelengths = np.tile(linelengths, len(positions))
1407         if len(linewidths) == 1:
1408             linewidths = np.tile(linewidths, len(positions))

1410             colors = list(colors) * len(positions)
1411         if len(alpha) == 1:
1412             alpha = list(alpha) * len(positions)

1414             linestyles = [linestyles] * len(positions)

1417             raise ValueError('lineoffsets and positions are unequal sized '
1418                              'sequences')
1419         if len(linelengths) != len(positions):
1420             raise ValueError('linelengths and positions are unequal sized '
1421                              'sequences')

1424                              'sequences')

1427                              'sequences')

1430                              'sequences')
1431         if len(linestyles) != len(positions):
1432             raise ValueError('linestyles and positions are unequal sized '
1433                              'sequences')

1435         colls = []
1436         for position, lineoffset, linelength, linewidth, color, alpha_, \
1437             linestyle in \
1438                 zip(positions, lineoffsets, linelengths, linewidths,
1439                     colors, alpha, linestyles):
1440             coll = mcoll.EventCollection(position,
1441                                          orientation=orientation,
1442                                          lineoffset=lineoffset,
1443                                          linelength=linelength,
1444                                          linewidth=linewidth,
1445                                          color=color,
1446                                          alpha=alpha_,
1447                                          linestyle=linestyle)

1449             coll._internal_update(kwargs)
1450             colls.append(coll)
1451 
1452         if len(positions) > 0:
1453             # try to get min/max
1454             min_max = [(np.min(_p), np.max(_p)) for _p in positions
1455                        if len(_p) > 0]
1456             # if we have any non-empty positions, try to autoscale
1457             if len(min_max) > 0:
1458                 mins, maxes = zip(*min_max)
1459                 minpos = np.min(mins)
1460                 maxpos = np.max(maxes)
1461 
1462                 minline = (lineoffsets - linelengths).min()
1463                 maxline = (lineoffsets + linelengths).max()
1464 
1465                 if orientation == "vertical":
1466                     corners = (minline, minpos), (maxline, maxpos)
1467                 else:  # "horizontal"
1468                     corners = (minpos, minline), (maxpos, maxline)
1469                 self.update_datalim(corners)
1470                 self._request_autoscale_view()
1471 
1472         return colls

1479     def plot(self, *args, scalex=True, scaley=True, data=None, **kwargs):
1480         """
1481         Plot y versus x as lines and/or markers.
1482 
1483         Call signatures::
1484 
1485             plot([x], y, [fmt], *, data=None, **kwargs)
1486             plot([x], y, [fmt], [x2], y2, [fmt2], ..., **kwargs)
1487 
1488         The coordinates of the points or line nodes are given by *x*, *y*.
1489 
1490         The optional parameter *fmt* is a convenient way for defining basic
1491         formatting like color, marker and linestyle. It's a shortcut string
1492         notation described in the *Notes* section below.
1493 
1494         >>> plot(x, y)        # plot x and y using default line style and color
1495         >>> plot(x, y, 'bo')  # plot x and y using blue circle markers
1496         >>> plot(y)           # plot y using x as index array 0..N-1
1497         >>> plot(y, 'r+')     # ditto, but with red plusses
1498 
1499         You can use `.Line2D` properties as keyword arguments for more
1500         control on the appearance. Line properties and *fmt* can be mixed.
1501         The following two calls yield identical results:
1502 
1503         >>> plot(x, y, 'go--', linewidth=2, markersize=12)
1504         >>> plot(x, y, color='green', marker='o', linestyle='dashed',
1505         ...      linewidth=2, markersize=12)
1506 
1507         When conflicting with *fmt*, keyword arguments take precedence.
1508 
1509 
1510         **Plotting labelled data**
1511 
1512         There's a convenient way for plotting objects with labelled data (i.e.
1513         data that can be accessed by index ``obj['y']``). Instead of giving
1514         the data in *x* and *y*, you can provide the object in the *data*
1515         parameter and just give the labels for *x* and *y*::
1516 
1517         >>> plot('xlabel', 'ylabel', data=obj)
1518 
1519         All indexable objects are supported. This could e.g. be a `dict`, a
1520         `pandas.DataFrame` or a structured numpy array.
1521 
1522 
1523         **Plotting multiple sets of data**
1524 
1525         There are various ways to plot multiple sets of data.
1526 
1527         - The most straight forward way is just to call `plot` multiple times.
1528           Example:
1529 
1530           >>> plot(x1, y1, 'bo')
1531           >>> plot(x2, y2, 'go')
1532 
1533         - If *x* and/or *y* are 2D arrays a separate data set will be drawn
1534           for every column. If both *x* and *y* are 2D, they must have the
1535           same shape. If only one of them is 2D with shape (N, m) the other
1536           must have length N and will be used for every data set m.
1537 
1538           Example:
1539 
1540           >>> x = [1, 2, 3]
1541           >>> y = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]])
1542           >>> plot(x, y)
1543 
1544           is equivalent to:
1545 
1546           >>> for col in range(y.shape[1]):
1547           ...     plot(x, y[:, col])
1548 
1549         - The third way is to specify multiple sets of *[x]*, *y*, *[fmt]*
1550           groups::
1551 
1552           >>> plot(x1, y1, 'g^', x2, y2, 'g-')
1553 
1554           In this case, any additional keyword argument applies to all
1555           datasets. Also, this syntax cannot be combined with the *data*
1556           parameter.
1557 
1558         By default, each line is assigned a different style specified by a
1559         'style cycle'. The *fmt* and line property parameters are only
1560         necessary if you want explicit deviations from these defaults.
1561         Alternatively, you can also change the style cycle using
1562         :rc:`axes.prop_cycle`.
1563 
1564 
1565         Parameters
1566         ----------
1567         x, y : array-like or scalar
1568             The horizontal / vertical coordinates of the data points.
1569             *x* values are optional and default to ``range(len(y))``.
1570 
1571             Commonly, these parameters are 1D arrays.
1572 
1573             They can also be scalars, or two-dimensional (in that case, the
1574             columns represent separate data sets).
1575 
1576             These arguments cannot be passed as keywords.
1577 
1578         fmt : str, optional
1579             A format string, e.g. 'ro' for red circles. See the *Notes*
1580             section for a full description of the format strings.
1581 
1582             Format strings are just an abbreviation for quickly setting
1583             basic line properties. All of these and more can also be
1584             controlled by keyword arguments.
1585 
1586             This argument cannot be passed as keyword.
1587 
1588         data : indexable object, optional
1589             An object with labelled data. If given, provide the label names to
1590             plot in *x* and *y*.
1591 
1592             .. note::
1593                 Technically there's a slight ambiguity in calls where the
1594                 second label is a valid *fmt*. ``plot('n', 'o', data=obj)``
1595                 could be ``plt(x, y)`` or ``plt(y, fmt)``. In such cases,
1596                 the former interpretation is chosen, but a warning is issued.
1597                 You may suppress the warning by adding an empty format string
1598                 ``plot('n', 'o', '', data=obj)``.
1599 
1600         Returns
1601         -------
1602         list of `.Line2D`
1603             A list of lines representing the plotted data.
1604 
1605         Other Parameters
1606         ----------------
1607         scalex, scaley : bool, default: True
1608             These parameters determine if the view limits are adapted to the
1609             data limits. The values are passed on to
1610             `~.axes.Axes.autoscale_view`.
1611 
1612         **kwargs : `.Line2D` properties, optional
1613             *kwargs* are used to specify properties like a line label (for
1614             auto legends), linewidth, antialiasing, marker face color.
1615             Example::
1616 
1617             >>> plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3], 'go-', label='line 1', linewidth=2)
1618             >>> plot([1, 2, 3], [1, 4, 9], 'rs', label='line 2')
1619 
1620             If you specify multiple lines with one plot call, the kwargs apply
1621             to all those lines. In case the label object is iterable, each
1622             element is used as labels for each set of data.
1623 
1624             Here is a list of available `.Line2D` properties:
1625 
1626             %(Line2D:kwdoc)s
1627 
1628         See Also
1629         --------
1630         scatter : XY scatter plot with markers of varying size and/or color (
1631             sometimes also called bubble chart).
1632 
1633         Notes
1634         -----
1635         **Format Strings**
1636 
1637         A format string consists of a part for color, marker and line::
1638 
1639             fmt = '[marker][line][color]'
1640 
1641         Each of them is optional. If not provided, the value from the style
1642         cycle is used. Exception: If ``line`` is given, but no ``marker``,
1643         the data will be a line without markers.
1644 
1645         Other combinations such as ``[color][marker][line]`` are also
1646         supported, but note that their parsing may be ambiguous.
1647 
1648         **Markers**
1649 
1650         =============   ===============================
1651         character       description
1652         =============   ===============================
1653         ``'.'``         point marker
1654         ``','``         pixel marker
1655         ``'o'``         circle marker
1656         ``'v'``         triangle_down marker
1657         ``'^'``         triangle_up marker
1658         ``'<'``         triangle_left marker
1659         ``'>'``         triangle_right marker
1660         ``'1'``         tri_down marker
1661         ``'2'``         tri_up marker
1662         ``'3'``         tri_left marker
1663         ``'4'``         tri_right marker
1664         ``'8'``         octagon marker
1665         ``'s'``         square marker
1666         ``'p'``         pentagon marker
1667         ``'P'``         plus (filled) marker
1668         ``'*'``         star marker
1669         ``'h'``         hexagon1 marker
1670         ``'H'``         hexagon2 marker
1671         ``'+'``         plus marker
1672         ``'x'``         x marker
1673         ``'X'``         x (filled) marker
1674         ``'D'``         diamond marker
1675         ``'d'``         thin_diamond marker
1676         ``'|'``         vline marker
1677         ``'_'``         hline marker
1678         =============   ===============================
1679 
1680         **Line Styles**
1681 
1682         =============    ===============================
1683         character        description
1684         =============    ===============================
1685         ``'-'``          solid line style
1686         ``'--'``         dashed line style
1687         ``'-.'``         dash-dot line style
1688         ``':'``          dotted line style
1689         =============    ===============================
1690 
1691         Example format strings::
1692 
1693             'b'    # blue markers with default shape
1694             'or'   # red circles
1695             '-g'   # green solid line
1696             '--'   # dashed line with default color
1697             '^k:'  # black triangle_up markers connected by a dotted line
1698 
1699         **Colors**
1700 
1701         The supported color abbreviations are the single letter codes
1702 
1703         =============    ===============================
1704         character        color
1705         =============    ===============================
1706         ``'b'``          blue
1707         ``'g'``          green
1708         ``'r'``          red
1709         ``'c'``          cyan
1710         ``'m'``          magenta
1711         ``'y'``          yellow
1712         ``'k'``          black
1713         ``'w'``          white
1714         =============    ===============================
1715 
1716         and the ``'CN'`` colors that index into the default property cycle.
1717 
1718         If the color is the only part of the format string, you can
1719         additionally use any  `matplotlib.colors` spec, e.g. full names
1720         (``'green'``) or hex strings (``'#008000'``).
1721         """
1722         kwargs = cbook.normalize_kwargs(kwargs, mlines.Line2D)
1723         lines = [*self._get_lines(*args, data=data, **kwargs)]
1724         for line in lines:
1725             self.add_line(line)
1726         if scalex:
1727             self._request_autoscale_view("x")
1728         if scaley:
1729             self._request_autoscale_view("y")
1730         return lines

2033     @_preprocess_data(replace_names=["x", "y"], label_namer="y")
2034     def xcorr(self, x, y, normed=True, detrend=mlab.detrend_none,
2035               usevlines=True, maxlags=10, **kwargs):
2036         r"""
2037         Plot the cross correlation between *x* and *y*.
2038 
2039         The correlation with lag k is defined as
2040         :math:`\sum_n x[n+k] \cdot y^*[n]`, where :math:`y^*` is the complex
2041         conjugate of :math:`y`.
2042 
2043         Parameters
2044         ----------
2045         x, y : array-like of length n
2046 
2047         detrend : callable, default: `.mlab.detrend_none` (no detrending)
2048             A detrending function applied to *x* and *y*.  It must have the
2049             signature ::
2050 
2051                 detrend(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
2052 
2053         normed : bool, default: True
2054             If ``True``, input vectors are normalised to unit length.
2055 
2056         usevlines : bool, default: True
2057             Determines the plot style.
2058 
2059             If ``True``, vertical lines are plotted from 0 to the xcorr value
2060             using `.Axes.vlines`. Additionally, a horizontal line is plotted
2061             at y=0 using `.Axes.axhline`.
2062 
2063             If ``False``, markers are plotted at the xcorr values using
2064             `.Axes.plot`.
2065 
2066         maxlags : int, default: 10
2067             Number of lags to show. If None, will return all ``2 * len(x) - 1``
2068             lags.
2069 
2070         Returns
2071         -------
2072         lags : array (length ``2*maxlags+1``)
2073             The lag vector.
2074         c : array  (length ``2*maxlags+1``)
2075             The auto correlation vector.
2076         line : `.LineCollection` or `.Line2D`
2077             `.Artist` added to the Axes of the correlation:
2078 
2079             - `.LineCollection` if *usevlines* is True.
2080             - `.Line2D` if *usevlines* is False.
2081         b : `.Line2D` or None
2082             Horizontal line at 0 if *usevlines* is True
2083             None *usevlines* is False.
2084 
2085         Other Parameters
2086         ----------------
2087         linestyle : `.Line2D` property, optional
2088             The linestyle for plotting the data points.
2089             Only used if *usevlines* is ``False``.
2090 
2091         marker : str, default: 'o'
2092             The marker for plotting the data points.
2093             Only used if *usevlines* is ``False``.
2094 
2095         data : indexable object, optional
2096             DATA_PARAMETER_PLACEHOLDER
2097 
2098         **kwargs
2099             Additional parameters are passed to `.Axes.vlines` and
2100             `.Axes.axhline` if *usevlines* is ``True``; otherwise they are
2101             passed to `.Axes.plot`.
2102 
2103         Notes
2104         -----
2105         The cross correlation is performed with `numpy.correlate` with
2106         ``mode = "full"``.
2107         """
2108         Nx = len(x)
2109         if Nx != len(y):
2110             raise ValueError('x and y must be equal length')
2111 
2112         x = detrend(np.asarray(x))
2113         y = detrend(np.asarray(y))
2114 
2115         correls = np.correlate(x, y, mode="full")
2116 
2117         if normed:
2118             correls = correls / np.sqrt(np.dot(x, x) * np.dot(y, y))
2119 
2120         if maxlags is None:
2121             maxlags = Nx - 1
2122 
2123         if maxlags >= Nx or maxlags < 1:
2124             raise ValueError('maxlags must be None or strictly '
2125                              'positive < %d' % Nx)
2126 
2127         lags = np.arange(-maxlags, maxlags + 1)
2128         correls = correls[Nx - 1 - maxlags:Nx + maxlags]
2129 
2130         if usevlines:
2131             a = self.vlines(lags, [0], correls, **kwargs)
2132             # Make label empty so only vertical lines get a legend entry
2133             kwargs.pop('label', '')
2134             b = self.axhline(**kwargs)
2135         else:
2136             kwargs.setdefault('marker', 'o')
2137             kwargs.setdefault('linestyle', 'None')
2138             a, = self.plot(lags, correls, **kwargs)
2139             b = None
2140         return lags, correls, a, b

2214     def _convert_dx(dx, x0, xconv, convert):
2215         """
2216         Small helper to do logic of width conversion flexibly.
2217 
2218         *dx* and *x0* have units, but *xconv* has already been converted
2219         to unitless (and is an ndarray).  This allows the *dx* to have units
2220         that are different from *x0*, but are still accepted by the
2221         ``__add__`` operator of *x0*.
2222         """
2223 
2224         # x should be an array...
2225         assert type(xconv) is np.ndarray
2226 
2227         if xconv.size == 0:
2228             # xconv has already been converted, but maybe empty...
2229             return convert(dx)
2230 
2231         try:
2232             # attempt to add the width to x0; this works for
2233             # datetime+timedelta, for instance
2234 
2235             # only use the first element of x and x0.  This saves
2236             # having to be sure addition works across the whole
2237             # vector.  This is particularly an issue if
2238             # x0 and dx are lists so x0 + dx just concatenates the lists.
2239             # We can't just cast x0 and dx to numpy arrays because that
2240             # removes the units from unit packages like `pint` that
2241             # wrap numpy arrays.
2242             try:
2243                 x0 = cbook._safe_first_finite(x0)
2244             except (TypeError, IndexError, KeyError):
2245                 pass
2246 
2247             try:
2248                 x = cbook._safe_first_finite(xconv)
2249             except (TypeError, IndexError, KeyError):
2250                 x = xconv
2251 
2252             delist = False
2253             if not np.iterable(dx):
2254                 dx = [dx]
2255                 delist = True
2256             dx = [convert(x0 + ddx) - x for ddx in dx]
2257             if delist:
2258                 dx = dx[0]
2259         except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):
2260             # if the above fails (for any reason) just fallback to what
2261             # we do by default and convert dx by itself.
2262             dx = convert(dx)
2263         return dx

2477         if len(patch_labels) != len(x):
2478             raise ValueError(f'number of labels ({len(patch_labels)}) '
2479                              f'does not match number of bars ({len(x)}).')
2480 
2481         linewidth = itertools.cycle(np.atleast_1d(linewidth))
2482         hatch = itertools.cycle(np.atleast_1d(hatch))
2483         color = itertools.chain(itertools.cycle(mcolors.to_rgba_array(color)),
2484                                 # Fallback if color == "none".
2485                                 itertools.repeat('none'))
2486         if edgecolor is None:
2487             edgecolor = itertools.repeat(None)
2488         else:
2489             edgecolor = itertools.chain(
2490                 itertools.cycle(mcolors.to_rgba_array(edgecolor)),
2491                 # Fallback if edgecolor == "none".
2492                 itertools.repeat('none'))
2493 
2494         # We will now resolve the alignment and really have
2495         # left, bottom, width, height vectors
2496         _api.check_in_list(['center', 'edge'], align=align)
2497         if align == 'center':
2498             if orientation == 'vertical':
2499                 try:
2500                     left = x - width / 2
2501                 except TypeError as e:
2502                     raise TypeError(f'the dtypes of parameters x ({x.dtype}) '
2503                                     f'and width ({width.dtype}) '
2504                                     f'are incompatible') from e
2505                 bottom = y
2506             else:  # horizontal
2507                 try:
2508                     bottom = y - height / 2
2509                 except TypeError as e:
2510                     raise TypeError(f'the dtypes of parameters y ({y.dtype}) '
2511                                     f'and height ({height.dtype}) '
2512                                     f'are incompatible') from e
2513                 left = x
2514         else:  # edge
2515             left = x
2516             bottom = y
2517 
2518         patches = []
2519         args = zip(left, bottom, width, height, color, edgecolor, linewidth,
2520                    hatch, patch_labels)
2521         for l, b, w, h, c, e, lw, htch, lbl in args:
2522             r = mpatches.Rectangle(
2523                 xy=(l, b), width=w, height=h,
2524                 facecolor=c,
2525                 edgecolor=e,
2526                 linewidth=lw,
2527                 label=lbl,
2528                 hatch=htch,
2529                 )
2530             r._internal_update(kwargs)
2531             r.get_path()._interpolation_steps = 100
2532             if orientation == 'vertical':
2533                 r.sticky_edges.y.append(b)
2534             else:  # horizontal
2535                 r.sticky_edges.x.append(l)
2536             self.add_patch(r)
2537             patches.append(r)
2538 
2539         if xerr is not None or yerr is not None:
2540             if orientation == 'vertical':
2541                 # using list comps rather than arrays to preserve unit info
2542                 ex = [l + 0.5 * w for l, w in zip(left, width)]
2543                 ey = [b + h for b, h in zip(bottom, height)]
2544 
2545             else:  # horizontal
2546                 # using list comps rather than arrays to preserve unit info
2547                 ex = [l + w for l, w in zip(left, width)]
2548                 ey = [b + 0.5 * h for b, h in zip(bottom, height)]
2549 
2550             error_kw.setdefault("label", '_nolegend_')
2551 
2552             errorbar = self.errorbar(ex, ey,
2553                                      yerr=yerr, xerr=xerr,
2554                                      fmt='none', **error_kw)
2555         else:
2556             errorbar = None
2557 
2558         self._request_autoscale_view()
2559 
2560         if orientation == 'vertical':
2561             datavalues = height
2562         else:  # horizontal
2563             datavalues = width
2564 
2565         bar_container = BarContainer(patches, errorbar, datavalues=datavalues,
2566                                      orientation=orientation,
2567                                      label=bar_container_label)
2568         self.add_container(bar_container)
2569 
2570         if tick_labels is not None:
2571             tick_labels = np.broadcast_to(tick_labels, len(patches))
2572             tick_label_axis.set_ticks(tick_label_position)
2573             tick_label_axis.set_ticklabels(tick_labels)
2574 
2575         return bar_container

2581         r"""
2582         Make a horizontal bar plot.
2583 
2584         The bars are positioned at *y* with the given *align*\ment. Their
2585         dimensions are given by *width* and *height*. The horizontal baseline
2586         is *left* (default 0).
2587 
2588         Many parameters can take either a single value applying to all bars
2589         or a sequence of values, one for each bar.
2590 
2591         Parameters
2592         ----------
2593         y : float or array-like
2594             The y coordinates of the bars. See also *align* for the
2595             alignment of the bars to the coordinates.
2596 
2597         width : float or array-like
2598             The width(s) of the bars.
2599 
2600             Note that if *left* has units (e.g. datetime), *width* should be in
2601             units that are a difference from the value of *left* (e.g. timedelta).
2602 
2603         height : float or array-like, default: 0.8
2604             The heights of the bars.
2605 
2606             Note that if *y* has units (e.g. datetime), then *height* should be in
2607             units that are a difference (e.g. timedelta) around the *y* values.
2608 
2609         left : float or array-like, default: 0
2610             The x coordinates of the left side(s) of the bars.
2611 
2612             Note that if *left* has units, then the x-axis will get a Locator and
2613             Formatter appropriate for the units (e.g. dates, or categorical).
2614 
2615         align : {'center', 'edge'}, default: 'center'
2616             Alignment of the base to the *y* coordinates*:
2617 
2618             - 'center': Center the bars on the *y* positions.
2619             - 'edge': Align the bottom edges of the bars with the *y*
2620               positions.
2621 
2622             To align the bars on the top edge pass a negative *height* and
2623             ``align='edge'``.
2624 
2625         Returns
2626         -------
2627         `.BarContainer`
2628             Container with all the bars and optionally errorbars.
2629 
2630         Other Parameters
2631         ----------------
2632         color : color or list of color, optional
2633             The colors of the bar faces.
2634 
2635         edgecolor : color or list of color, optional
2636             The colors of the bar edges.
2637 
2638         linewidth : float or array-like, optional
2639             Width of the bar edge(s). If 0, don't draw edges.
2640 
2641         tick_label : str or list of str, optional
2642             The tick labels of the bars.
2643             Default: None (Use default numeric labels.)
2644 
2645         label : str or list of str, optional
2646             A single label is attached to the resulting `.BarContainer` as a
2647             label for the whole dataset.

2649             labels the individual bars. Repeated labels are not de-duplicated
2650             and will cause repeated label entries, so this is best used when
2651             bars also differ in style (e.g., by passing a list to *color*.)

2704     def bar_label(self, container, labels=None, *, fmt="%g", label_type="edge",
2705                   padding=0, **kwargs):
2706         """
2707         Label a bar plot.
2708 
2709         Adds labels to bars in the given `.BarContainer`.
2710         You may need to adjust the axis limits to fit the labels.
2711 
2712         Parameters
2713         ----------
2714         container : `.BarContainer`
2715             Container with all the bars and optionally errorbars, likely
2716             returned from `.bar` or `.barh`.
2717 
2718         labels : array-like, optional
2719             A list of label texts, that should be displayed. If not given, the
2720             label texts will be the data values formatted with *fmt*.
2721 
2722         fmt : str or callable, default: '%g'
2723             An unnamed %-style or {}-style format string for the label or a
2724             function to call with the value as the first argument.
2725             When *fmt* is a string and can be interpreted in both formats,
2726             %-style takes precedence over {}-style.
2727 
2728             .. versionadded:: 3.7
2729                Support for {}-style format string and callables.
2730 
2731         label_type : {'edge', 'center'}, default: 'edge'
2732             The label type. Possible values:
2733 
2734             - 'edge': label placed at the end-point of the bar segment, and the
2735               value displayed will be the position of that end-point.
2736             - 'center': label placed in the center of the bar segment, and the
2737               value displayed will be the length of that segment.
2738               (useful for stacked bars, i.e.,
2739               :doc:`/gallery/lines_bars_and_markers/bar_label_demo`)
2740 
2741         padding : float, default: 0
2742             Distance of label from the end of the bar, in points.
2743 
2744         **kwargs
2745             Any remaining keyword arguments are passed through to
2746             `.Axes.annotate`. The alignment parameters (
2747             *horizontalalignment* / *ha*, *verticalalignment* / *va*) are
2748             not supported because the labels are automatically aligned to
2749             the bars.
2750 
2751         Returns
2752         -------
2753         list of `.Text`
2754             A list of `.Text` instances for the labels.
2755         """
2756         for key in ['horizontalalignment', 'ha', 'verticalalignment', 'va']:
2757             if key in kwargs:
2758                 raise ValueError(
2759                     f"Passing {key!r} to bar_label() is not supported.")
2760 
2761         a, b = self.yaxis.get_view_interval()
2762         y_inverted = a > b
2763         c, d = self.xaxis.get_view_interval()
2764         x_inverted = c > d
2765 
2766         # want to know whether to put label on positive or negative direction
2767         # cannot use np.sign here because it will return 0 if x == 0
2768         def sign(x):
2769             return 1 if x >= 0 else -1
2770 
2771         _api.check_in_list(['edge', 'center'], label_type=label_type)
2772 
2773         bars = container.patches
2774         errorbar = container.errorbar
2775         datavalues = container.datavalues
2776         orientation = container.orientation
2777 
2778         if errorbar:
2779             # check "ErrorbarContainer" for the definition of these elements
2780             lines = errorbar.lines  # attribute of "ErrorbarContainer" (tuple)
2781             barlinecols = lines[2]  # 0: data_line, 1: caplines, 2: barlinecols
2782             barlinecol = barlinecols[0]  # the "LineCollection" of error bars
2783             errs = barlinecol.get_segments()
2784         else:
2785             errs = []
2786 
2787         if labels is None:
2788             labels = []
2789 
2790         annotations = []
2791 
2792         for bar, err, dat, lbl in itertools.zip_longest(
2793                 bars, errs, datavalues, labels
2794         ):
2795             (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = bar.get_bbox().get_points()
2796             xc, yc = (x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2
2797 
2798             if orientation == "vertical":
2799                 extrema = max(y0, y1) if dat >= 0 else min(y0, y1)
2800                 length = abs(y0 - y1)
2801             else:  # horizontal
2802                 extrema = max(x0, x1) if dat >= 0 else min(x0, x1)
2803                 length = abs(x0 - x1)
2804 
2805             if err is None or np.size(err) == 0:
2806                 endpt = extrema
2807             elif orientation == "vertical":
2808                 endpt = err[:, 1].max() if dat >= 0 else err[:, 1].min()
2809             else:  # horizontal
2810                 endpt = err[:, 0].max() if dat >= 0 else err[:, 0].min()
2811 
2812             if label_type == "center":
2813                 value = sign(dat) * length
2814             else:  # edge
2815                 value = extrema
2816 
2817             if label_type == "center":
2818                 xy = (0.5, 0.5)
2819                 kwargs["xycoords"] = (
2820                     lambda r, b=bar:
2821                         mtransforms.Bbox.intersection(
2822                             b.get_window_extent(r), b.get_clip_box()
2823                         ) or mtransforms.Bbox.null()
2824                 )
2825             else:  # edge
2826                 if orientation == "vertical":
2827                     xy = xc, endpt
2828                 else:  # horizontal
2829                     xy = endpt, yc
2830 
2831             if orientation == "vertical":
2832                 y_direction = -1 if y_inverted else 1
2833                 xytext = 0, y_direction * sign(dat) * padding
2834             else:  # horizontal
2835                 x_direction = -1 if x_inverted else 1
2836                 xytext = x_direction * sign(dat) * padding, 0
2837 
2838             if label_type == "center":
2839                 ha, va = "center", "center"
2840             else:  # edge
2841                 if orientation == "vertical":
2842                     ha = 'center'
2843                     if y_inverted:
2844                         va = 'top' if dat > 0 else 'bottom'  # also handles NaN
2845                     else:
2846                         va = 'top' if dat < 0 else 'bottom'  # also handles NaN
2847                 else:  # horizontal
2848                     if x_inverted:
2849                         ha = 'right' if dat > 0 else 'left'  # also handles NaN
2850                     else:
2851                         ha = 'right' if dat < 0 else 'left'  # also handles NaN
2852                     va = 'center'
2853 
2854             if np.isnan(dat):
2855                 lbl = ''
2856 
2857             if lbl is None:
2858                 if isinstance(fmt, str):
2859                     lbl = cbook._auto_format_str(fmt, value)
2860                 elif callable(fmt):
2861                     lbl = fmt(value)
2862                 else:
2863                     raise TypeError("fmt must be a str or callable")
2864             annotation = self.annotate(lbl,
2865                                        xy, xytext, textcoords="offset points",
2866                                        ha=ha, va=va, **kwargs)
2867             annotations.append(annotation)
2868 
2869         return annotations
