386     def _get_validation_exclusions(self):
387         """
388         For backwards-compatibility, exclude several types of fields from model
389         validation. See tickets #12507, #12521, #12553.
390         """
391         exclude = set()
392         # Build up a list of fields that should be excluded from model field
393         # validation and unique checks.
394         for f in self.instance._meta.fields:
395             field = f.name
396             # Exclude fields that aren't on the form. The developer may be
397             # adding these values to the model after form validation.
398             if field not in self.fields:
399                 exclude.add(f.name)
400 
401             # Don't perform model validation on fields that were defined
402             # manually on the form and excluded via the ModelForm's Meta
403             # class. See #12901.
404             elif self._meta.fields and field not in self._meta.fields:
405                 exclude.add(f.name)
406             elif self._meta.exclude and field in self._meta.exclude:
407                 exclude.add(f.name)
408 
409             # Exclude fields that failed form validation. There's no need for
410             # the model fields to validate them as well.
411             elif field in self._errors:
412                 exclude.add(f.name)
413 
414             # Exclude empty fields that are not required by the form, if the
415             # underlying model field is required. This keeps the model field
416             # from raising a required error. Note: don't exclude the field from
417             # validation if the model field allows blanks. If it does, the blank
418             # value may be included in a unique check, so cannot be excluded
419             # from validation.
420             else:
421                 form_field = self.fields[field]
422                 field_value = self.cleaned_data.get(field)
423                 if (
424                     not f.blank
425                     and not form_field.required
426                     and field_value in form_field.empty_values
427                 ):
428                     exclude.add(f.name)
429         return exclude
430 
431     def clean(self):
432         self._validate_unique = True
433         return self.cleaned_data
434 
435     def _update_errors(self, errors):
436         # Override any validation error messages defined at the model level
437         # with those defined at the form level.
438         opts = self._meta
439 
440         # Allow the model generated by construct_instance() to raise
441         # ValidationError and have them handled in the same way as others.
442         if hasattr(errors, "error_dict"):
443             error_dict = errors.error_dict
444         else:
445             error_dict = {NON_FIELD_ERRORS: errors}
446 
447         for field, messages in error_dict.items():
448             if (
449                 field == NON_FIELD_ERRORS
450                 and opts.error_messages
451                 and NON_FIELD_ERRORS in opts.error_messages
452             ):
453                 error_messages = opts.error_messages[NON_FIELD_ERRORS]
454             elif field in self.fields:
455                 error_messages = self.fields[field].error_messages
456             else:
457                 continue
458 
459             for message in messages:
460                 if (
461                     isinstance(message, ValidationError)
462                     and message.code in error_messages
463                 ):
464                     message.message = error_messages[message.code]
465 
466         self.add_error(None, errors)
467 
468     def _post_clean(self):
469         opts = self._meta
470 
471         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
472 
473         # Foreign Keys being used to represent inline relationships
474         # are excluded from basic field value validation. This is for two
475         # reasons: firstly, the value may not be supplied (#12507; the
476         # case of providing new values to the admin); secondly the
477         # object being referred to may not yet fully exist (#12749).
478         # However, these fields *must* be included in uniqueness checks,
479         # so this can't be part of _get_validation_exclusions().
480         for name, field in self.fields.items():
481             if isinstance(field, InlineForeignKeyField):
482                 exclude.add(name)
483 
484         try:
485             self.instance = construct_instance(
486                 self, self.instance, opts.fields, opts.exclude
487             )
488         except ValidationError as e:
489             self._update_errors(e)
490 
491         try:
492             self.instance.full_clean(exclude=exclude, validate_unique=False)
493         except ValidationError as e:
494             self._update_errors(e)
495 
496         # Validate uniqueness if needed.
497         if self._validate_unique:
498             self.validate_unique()
499 
500     def validate_unique(self):
501         """
502         Call the instance's validate_unique() method and update the form's
503         validation errors if any were raised.
504         """
505         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
506         try:
507             self.instance.validate_unique(exclude=exclude)
508         except ValidationError as e:
509             self._update_errors(e)
510 
511     def _save_m2m(self):
512         """
513         Save the many-to-many fields and generic relations for this form.
514         """
515         cleaned_data = self.cleaned_data
516         exclude = self._meta.exclude
517         fields = self._meta.fields
518         opts = self.instance._meta
519         # Note that for historical reasons we want to include also
520         # private_fields here. (GenericRelation was previously a fake
521         # m2m field).
522         for f in chain(opts.many_to_many, opts.private_fields):
523             if not hasattr(f, "save_form_data"):
524                 continue
525             if fields and f.name not in fields:
526                 continue
527             if exclude and f.name in exclude:
528                 continue
529             if f.name in cleaned_data:
530                 f.save_form_data(self.instance, cleaned_data[f.name])
531 
532     def save(self, commit=True):
533         """
534         Save this form's self.instance object if commit=True. Otherwise, add
535         a save_m2m() method to the form which can be called after the instance
536         is saved manually at a later time. Return the model instance.
537         """
538         if self.errors:
539             raise ValueError(
540                 "The %s could not be %s because the data didn't validate."
541                 % (
542                     self.instance._meta.object_name,
543                     "created" if self.instance._state.adding else "changed",
544                 )
545             )
546         if commit:
547             # If committing, save the instance and the m2m data immediately.
548             self.instance.save()
549             self._save_m2m()
550         else:
551             # If not committing, add a method to the form to allow deferred
552             # saving of m2m data.
553             self.save_m2m = self._save_m2m
554         return self.instance
555 
556     save.alters_data = True

563 def modelform_factory(
564     model,
565     form=ModelForm,
566     fields=None,
567     exclude=None,
568     formfield_callback=None,
569     widgets=None,
570     localized_fields=None,
571     labels=None,
572     help_texts=None,
573     error_messages=None,
574     field_classes=None,
575 ):
576     """
577     Return a ModelForm containing form fields for the given model. You can
578     optionally pass a `form` argument to use as a starting point for
579     constructing the ModelForm.
580 
581     ``fields`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, include only
582     the named fields in the returned fields. If omitted or '__all__', use all
583     fields.
584 
585     ``exclude`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, exclude the
586     named fields from the returned fields, even if they are listed in the
587     ``fields`` argument.
588 
589     ``widgets`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a widget.
590 
591     ``localized_fields`` is a list of names of fields which should be localized.
592 
593     ``formfield_callback`` is a callable that takes a model field and returns
594     a form field.
595 
596     ``labels`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a label.
597 
598     ``help_texts`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a help text.
599 
600     ``error_messages`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a
601     dictionary of error messages.
602 
603     ``field_classes`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a form
604     field class.
605     """
606     # Create the inner Meta class. FIXME: ideally, we should be able to
607     # construct a ModelForm without creating and passing in a temporary
608     # inner class.
609 
610     # Build up a list of attributes that the Meta object will have.
611     attrs = {"model": model}
612     if fields is not None:
613         attrs["fields"] = fields
614     if exclude is not None:
615         attrs["exclude"] = exclude
616     if widgets is not None:
617         attrs["widgets"] = widgets
618     if localized_fields is not None:
619         attrs["localized_fields"] = localized_fields
620     if labels is not None:
621         attrs["labels"] = labels
622     if help_texts is not None:
623         attrs["help_texts"] = help_texts
624     if error_messages is not None:
625         attrs["error_messages"] = error_messages
626     if field_classes is not None:
627         attrs["field_classes"] = field_classes
628 
629     # If parent form class already has an inner Meta, the Meta we're
630     # creating needs to inherit from the parent's inner meta.
631     bases = (form.Meta,) if hasattr(form, "Meta") else ()
632     Meta = type("Meta", bases, attrs)
633     if formfield_callback:
634         Meta.formfield_callback = staticmethod(formfield_callback)
635     # Give this new form class a reasonable name.
636     class_name = model.__name__ + "Form"
637 
638     # Class attributes for the new form class.
639     form_class_attrs = {"Meta": Meta, "formfield_callback": formfield_callback}
640 
641     if getattr(Meta, "fields", None) is None and getattr(Meta, "exclude", None) is None:
642         raise ImproperlyConfigured(
643             "Calling modelform_factory without defining 'fields' or "
644             "'exclude' explicitly is prohibited."
645         )
646 
647     # Instantiate type(form) in order to use the same metaclass as form.
648     return type(form)(class_name, (form,), form_class_attrs)

654 class BaseModelFormSet(BaseFormSet):
655     """
656     A ``FormSet`` for editing a queryset and/or adding new objects to it.
657     """
658 
659     model = None
660     edit_only = False
661 
662     # Set of fields that must be unique among forms of this set.
663     unique_fields = set()
664 
665     def __init__(
666         self,
667         data=None,
668         files=None,
669         auto_id="id_%s",
670         prefix=None,
671         queryset=None,
672         *,
673         initial=None,
674         **kwargs,
675     ):
676         self.queryset = queryset
677         self.initial_extra = initial
678         super().__init__(
679             **{
680                 "data": data,
681                 "files": files,
682                 "auto_id": auto_id,
683                 "prefix": prefix,
684                 **kwargs,
685             }
686         )
687 
688     def initial_form_count(self):
689         """Return the number of forms that are required in this FormSet."""
690         if not self.is_bound:
691             return len(self.get_queryset())
692         return super().initial_form_count()
693 
694     def _existing_object(self, pk):
695         if not hasattr(self, "_object_dict"):
696             self._object_dict = {o.pk: o for o in self.get_queryset()}
697         return self._object_dict.get(pk)
698 
699     def _get_to_python(self, field):
700         """
701         If the field is a related field, fetch the concrete field's (that
702         is, the ultimate pointed-to field's) to_python.
703         """
704         while field.remote_field is not None:
705             field = field.remote_field.get_related_field()
706         return field.to_python
707 
708     def _construct_form(self, i, **kwargs):
709         pk_required = i < self.initial_form_count()
710         if pk_required:
711             if self.is_bound:
712                 pk_key = "%s-%s" % (self.add_prefix(i), self.model._meta.pk.name)
713                 try:
714                     pk = self.data[pk_key]
715                 except KeyError:
716                     # The primary key is missing. The user may have tampered
717                     # with POST data.
718                     pass
719                 else:
720                     to_python = self._get_to_python(self.model._meta.pk)
721                     try:
722                         pk = to_python(pk)
723                     except ValidationError:

797     def validate_unique(self):
798         # Collect unique_checks and date_checks to run from all the forms.
799         all_unique_checks = set()
800         all_date_checks = set()
801         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
802         valid_forms = [
803             form
804             for form in self.forms
805             if form.is_valid() and form not in forms_to_delete
806         ]
807         for form in valid_forms:
808             exclude = form._get_validation_exclusions()
809             unique_checks, date_checks = form.instance._get_unique_checks(
810                 exclude=exclude,
811                 include_meta_constraints=True,
812             )
813             all_unique_checks.update(unique_checks)
814             all_date_checks.update(date_checks)
815 
816         errors = []
817         # Do each of the unique checks (unique and unique_together)
818         for uclass, unique_check in all_unique_checks:
819             seen_data = set()
820             for form in valid_forms:
821                 # Get the data for the set of fields that must be unique among
822                 # the forms.
823                 row_data = (
824                     field if field in self.unique_fields else form.cleaned_data[field]
825                     for field in unique_check
826                     if field in form.cleaned_data
827                 )
828                 # Reduce Model instances to their primary key values
829                 row_data = tuple(
830                     d._get_pk_val() if hasattr(d, "_get_pk_val")
831                     # Prevent "unhashable type: list" errors later on.
832                     else tuple(d) if isinstance(d, list) else d
833                     for d in row_data
834                 )
835                 if row_data and None not in row_data:
836                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
837                     if row_data in seen_data:
838                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
839                         # the form as invalid
840                         errors.append(self.get_unique_error_message(unique_check))
841                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class(
842                             [self.get_form_error()],
843                             renderer=self.renderer,
844                         )
845                         # Remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it
846                         # was invalid.
847                         for field in unique_check:
848                             if field in form.cleaned_data:
849                                 del form.cleaned_data[field]
850                     # mark the data as seen
851                     seen_data.add(row_data)
852         # iterate over each of the date checks now
853         for date_check in all_date_checks:
854             seen_data = set()
855             uclass, lookup, field, unique_for = date_check
856             for form in valid_forms:
857                 # see if we have data for both fields
858                 if (
859                     form.cleaned_data
860                     and form.cleaned_data[field] is not None
861                     and form.cleaned_data[unique_for] is not None
862                 ):
863                     # if it's a date lookup we need to get the data for all the fields
864                     if lookup == "date":
865                         date = form.cleaned_data[unique_for]
866                         date_data = (date.year, date.month, date.day)
867                     # otherwise it's just the attribute on the date/datetime
868                     # object
869                     else:
870                         date_data = (getattr(form.cleaned_data[unique_for], lookup),)
871                     data = (form.cleaned_data[field],) + date_data
872                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
873                     if data in seen_data:
874                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
875                         # the form as invalid
876                         errors.append(self.get_date_error_message(date_check))
877                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class(
878                             [self.get_form_error()],
879                             renderer=self.renderer,
880                         )
881                         # Remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it
882                         # was invalid.
883                         del form.cleaned_data[field]
884                     # mark the data as seen
885                     seen_data.add(data)
886 
887         if errors:
888             raise ValidationError(errors)
889 
890     def get_unique_error_message(self, unique_check):
891         if len(unique_check) == 1:
892             return gettext("Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s.") % {
893                 "field": unique_check[0],
894             }
895         else:
896             return gettext(
897                 "Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s, which must be unique."
898             ) % {
899                 "field": get_text_list(unique_check, _("and")),
900             }

902     def get_date_error_message(self, date_check):

904             "Please correct the duplicate data for %(field_name)s "
905             "which must be unique for the %(lookup)s in %(date_field)s."
906         ) % {
907             "field_name": date_check[2],
908             "date_field": date_check[3],

915     def save_existing_objects(self, commit=True):
916         self.changed_objects = []
917         self.deleted_objects = []
918         if not self.initial_forms:
919             return []
920 
921         saved_instances = []
922         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
923         for form in self.initial_forms:
924             obj = form.instance
925             # If the pk is None, it means either:
926             # 1. The object is an unexpected empty model, created by invalid
927             #    POST data such as an object outside the formset's queryset.
928             # 2. The object was already deleted from the database.
929             if obj.pk is None:
930                 continue
931             if form in forms_to_delete:
932                 self.deleted_objects.append(obj)
933                 self.delete_existing(obj, commit=commit)
934             elif form.has_changed():
935                 self.changed_objects.append((obj, form.changed_data))
936                 saved_instances.append(self.save_existing(form, obj, commit=commit))
937                 if not commit:
938                     self.saved_forms.append(form)

947             # object.

949                 continue

951             if not commit:
952                 self.saved_forms.append(form)

955     def add_fields(self, form, index):
956         """Add a hidden field for the object's primary key."""
957         from django.db.models import AutoField, ForeignKey, OneToOneField
958 
959         self._pk_field = pk = self.model._meta.pk
960         # If a pk isn't editable, then it won't be on the form, so we need to
961         # add it here so we can tell which object is which when we get the
962         # data back. Generally, pk.editable should be false, but for some
963         # reason, auto_created pk fields and AutoField's editable attribute is
964         # True, so check for that as well.
965 
966         def pk_is_not_editable(pk):
967             return (
968                 (not pk.editable)
969                 or (pk.auto_created or isinstance(pk, AutoField))
970                 or (
971                     pk.remote_field
972                     and pk.remote_field.parent_link
973                     and pk_is_not_editable(pk.remote_field.model._meta.pk)
974                 )
975             )
976 
977         if pk_is_not_editable(pk) or pk.name not in form.fields:
978             if form.is_bound:
979                 # If we're adding the related instance, ignore its primary key
980                 # as it could be an auto-generated default which isn't actually
981                 # in the database.
982                 pk_value = None if form.instance._state.adding else form.instance.pk
983             else:
984                 try:
985                     if index is not None:
986                         pk_value = self.get_queryset()[index].pk
987                     else:
988                         pk_value = None
989                 except IndexError:
990                     pk_value = None
991             if isinstance(pk, (ForeignKey, OneToOneField)):
992                 qs = pk.remote_field.model._default_manager.get_queryset()
993             else:
994                 qs = self.model._default_manager.get_queryset()
995             qs = qs.using(form.instance._state.db)
996             if form._meta.widgets:
997                 widget = form._meta.widgets.get(self._pk_field.name, HiddenInput)
998             else:
999                 widget = HiddenInput
1000             form.fields[self._pk_field.name] = ModelChoiceField(
1001                 qs, initial=pk_value, required=False, widget=widget
1002             )
1003         super().add_fields(form, index)

1103 
1104         # Add the generated field to form._meta.fields if it's defined to make
1105         # sure validation isn't skipped on that field.

1188 def _get_foreign_key(parent_model, model, fk_name=None, can_fail=False):
1189     """
1190     Find and return the ForeignKey from model to parent if there is one
1191     (return None if can_fail is True and no such field exists). If fk_name is
1192     provided, assume it is the name of the ForeignKey field. Unless can_fail is
1193     True, raise an exception if there isn't a ForeignKey from model to
1194     parent_model.
1195     """
1196     # avoid circular import
1197     from django.db.models import ForeignKey
1198 
1199     opts = model._meta
1200     if fk_name:
1201         fks_to_parent = [f for f in opts.fields if f.name == fk_name]
1202         if len(fks_to_parent) == 1:
1203             fk = fks_to_parent[0]
1204             parent_list = parent_model._meta.get_parent_list()
1205             if (
1206                 not isinstance(fk, ForeignKey)
1207                 or (
1208                     # ForeignKey to proxy models.
1209                     fk.remote_field.model._meta.proxy
1210                     and fk.remote_field.model._meta.proxy_for_model not in parent_list
1211                 )
1212                 or (
1213                     # ForeignKey to concrete models.
1214                     not fk.remote_field.model._meta.proxy
1215                     and fk.remote_field.model != parent_model
1216                     and fk.remote_field.model not in parent_list
1217                 )
1218             ):
1219                 raise ValueError(
1220                     "fk_name '%s' is not a ForeignKey to '%s'."
1221                     % (fk_name, parent_model._meta.label)
1222                 )
1223         elif not fks_to_parent:
1224             raise ValueError(
1225                 "'%s' has no field named '%s'." % (model._meta.label, fk_name)
1226             )
1227     else:
1228         # Try to discover what the ForeignKey from model to parent_model is
1229         parent_list = parent_model._meta.get_parent_list()
1230         fks_to_parent = [
1231             f
1232             for f in opts.fields
1233             if isinstance(f, ForeignKey)
1234             and (
1235                 f.remote_field.model == parent_model
1236                 or f.remote_field.model in parent_list
1237                 or (
1238                     f.remote_field.model._meta.proxy
1239                     and f.remote_field.model._meta.proxy_for_model in parent_list
1240                 )
1241             )
1242         ]
1243         if len(fks_to_parent) == 1:
1244             fk = fks_to_parent[0]
1245         elif not fks_to_parent:
1246             if can_fail:
1247                 return
1248             raise ValueError(
1249                 "'%s' has no ForeignKey to '%s'."
1250                 % (
1251                     model._meta.label,
1252                     parent_model._meta.label,
1253                 )
1254             )
1255         else:
1256             raise ValueError(
1257                 "'%s' has more than one ForeignKey to '%s'. You must specify "
1258                 "a 'fk_name' attribute."
1259                 % (
1260                     model._meta.label,
1261                     parent_model._meta.label,
1262                 )
1263             )
1264     return fk

195             gradients, hessians = self.loss_.init_gradients_and_hessians(
196                 n_samples=n_samples,
197                 prediction_dim=self.n_trees_per_iteration_
198             )
199 
200             # predictors is a matrix (list of lists) of TreePredictor objects
201             # with shape (n_iter_, n_trees_per_iteration)
202             self._predictors = predictors = []
203 
204             # Initialize structures and attributes related to early stopping
205             self.scorer_ = None  # set if scoring != loss
206             raw_predictions_val = None  # set if scoring == loss and use val
207             self.train_score_ = []
208             self.validation_score_ = []
209 
210             if self.do_early_stopping_:
211                 # populate train_score and validation_score with the
212                 # predictions of the initial model (before the first tree)
213 
214                 if self.scoring == 'loss':
215                     # we're going to compute scoring w.r.t the loss. As losses
216                     # take raw predictions as input (unlike the scorers), we
217                     # can optimize a bit and avoid repeating computing the
218                     # predictions of the previous trees. We'll re-use
219                     # raw_predictions (as it's needed for training anyway) for
220                     # evaluating the training loss, and create
221                     # raw_predictions_val for storing the raw predictions of
222                     # the validation data.
223 
224                     if self._use_validation_data:
225                         raw_predictions_val = np.zeros(
226                             shape=(self.n_trees_per_iteration_,
227                                    X_binned_val.shape[0]),
228                             dtype=self._baseline_prediction.dtype
229                         )
230 
231                         raw_predictions_val += self._baseline_prediction
232 
233                     self._check_early_stopping_loss(raw_predictions, y_train,
234                                                     raw_predictions_val, y_val)
235                 else:
236                     self.scorer_ = check_scoring(self, self.scoring)
237                     # scorer_ is a callable with signature (est, X, y) and
238                     # calls est.predict() or est.predict_proba() depending on
239                     # its nature.
240                     # Unfortunately, each call to scorer_() will compute
241                     # the predictions of all the trees. So we use a subset of
242                     # the training set to compute train scores.
243 
244                     # Save the seed for the small trainset generator
245                     self._small_trainset_seed = rng.randint(1024)
246 
247                     # Compute the subsample set
248                     (X_binned_small_train,
249                      y_small_train) = self._get_small_trainset(
250                         X_binned_train, y_train, self._small_trainset_seed)
251 
252                     self._check_early_stopping_scorer(
253                         X_binned_small_train, y_small_train,
254                         X_binned_val, y_val,
255                     )
256             begin_at_stage = 0
257 
258         # warm start: this is not the first time fit was called
259         else:
260             # Check that the maximum number of iterations is not smaller
261             # than the number of iterations from the previous fit
262             if self.max_iter < self.n_iter_:
263                 raise ValueError(
264                     'max_iter=%d must be larger than or equal to '
265                     'n_iter_=%d when warm_start==True'
266                     % (self.max_iter, self.n_iter_)
267                 )
268 
269             # Convert array attributes to lists
270             self.train_score_ = self.train_score_.tolist()
271             self.validation_score_ = self.validation_score_.tolist()
272 
273             # Compute raw predictions
274             raw_predictions = self._raw_predict(X_binned_train)
275 
276             if self.do_early_stopping_ and self.scoring != 'loss':
277                 # Compute the subsample set
278                 X_binned_small_train, y_small_train = self._get_small_trainset(
279                     X_binned_train, y_train, self._small_trainset_seed)
280 
281             # Initialize the gradients and hessians
282             gradients, hessians = self.loss_.init_gradients_and_hessians(
283                 n_samples=n_samples,
284                 prediction_dim=self.n_trees_per_iteration_
285             )
286 
287             # Get the predictors from the previous fit
288             predictors = self._predictors
289 
290             begin_at_stage = self.n_iter_
291 
292         for iteration in range(begin_at_stage, self.max_iter):
293 
294             if self.verbose:
295                 iteration_start_time = time()
296                 print("[{}/{}] ".format(iteration + 1, self.max_iter),
297                       end='', flush=True)
298 
299             # Update gradients and hessians, inplace
300             self.loss_.update_gradients_and_hessians(gradients, hessians,
301                                                      y_train, raw_predictions)
302 
303             # Append a list since there may be more than 1 predictor per iter
304             predictors.append([])
305 
306             # Build `n_trees_per_iteration` trees.
307             for k in range(self.n_trees_per_iteration_):
308 
309                 grower = TreeGrower(
310                     X_binned_train, gradients[k, :], hessians[k, :],
311                     n_bins=n_bins,
312                     n_bins_non_missing=self.bin_mapper_.n_bins_non_missing_,
313                     has_missing_values=has_missing_values,
314                     max_leaf_nodes=self.max_leaf_nodes,
315                     max_depth=self.max_depth,
316                     min_samples_leaf=self.min_samples_leaf,
317                     l2_regularization=self.l2_regularization,
318                     shrinkage=self.learning_rate)
319                 grower.grow()
320 
321                 acc_apply_split_time += grower.total_apply_split_time
322                 acc_find_split_time += grower.total_find_split_time
323                 acc_compute_hist_time += grower.total_compute_hist_time
324 
325                 predictor = grower.make_predictor(
326                     bin_thresholds=self.bin_mapper_.bin_thresholds_
327                 )
328                 predictors[-1].append(predictor)
329 
330                 # Update raw_predictions with the predictions of the newly
331                 # created tree.
332                 tic_pred = time()
333                 _update_raw_predictions(raw_predictions[k, :], grower)
334                 toc_pred = time()
335                 acc_prediction_time += toc_pred - tic_pred
336 
337             should_early_stop = False
338             if self.do_early_stopping_:
339                 if self.scoring == 'loss':
340                     # Update raw_predictions_val with the newest tree(s)
341                     if self._use_validation_data:
342                         for k, pred in enumerate(self._predictors[-1]):
343                             raw_predictions_val[k, :] += (
344                                 pred.predict_binned(
345                                     X_binned_val,
346                                     self.bin_mapper_.missing_values_bin_idx_
347                                 )
348                             )
349 
350                     should_early_stop = self._check_early_stopping_loss(
351                         raw_predictions, y_train,
352                         raw_predictions_val, y_val
353                     )
354 
355                 else:
356                     should_early_stop = self._check_early_stopping_scorer(
357                         X_binned_small_train, y_small_train,
358                         X_binned_val, y_val,
359                     )
360 
361             if self.verbose:
362                 self._print_iteration_stats(iteration_start_time)
363 
364             # maybe we could also early stop if all the trees are stumps?
365             if should_early_stop:
366                 break
367 
368         if self.verbose:
369             duration = time() - fit_start_time
370             n_total_leaves = sum(
371                 predictor.get_n_leaf_nodes()
372                 for predictors_at_ith_iteration in self._predictors
373                 for predictor in predictors_at_ith_iteration
374             )
375             n_predictors = sum(
376                 len(predictors_at_ith_iteration)
377                 for predictors_at_ith_iteration in self._predictors)
378             print("Fit {} trees in {:.3f} s, ({} total leaves)".format(
379                 n_predictors, duration, n_total_leaves))
380             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent computing histograms:',
381                                           acc_compute_hist_time))
382             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent finding best splits:',
383                                           acc_find_split_time))
384             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent applying splits:',
385                                           acc_apply_split_time))
386             print("{:<32} {:.3f}s".format('Time spent predicting:',
387                                           acc_prediction_time))
388 
389         self.train_score_ = np.asarray(self.train_score_)
390         self.validation_score_ = np.asarray(self.validation_score_)
391         del self._in_fit  # hard delete so we're sure it can't be used anymore
392         return self
393 
394     def _is_fitted(self):
395         return len(getattr(self, '_predictors', [])) > 0
396 
397     def _clear_state(self):
398         """Clear the state of the gradient boosting model."""
399         for var in ('train_score_', 'validation_score_', '_rng'):
400             if hasattr(self, var):
401                 delattr(self, var)
402 
403     def _get_small_trainset(self, X_binned_train, y_train, seed):
404         """Compute the indices of the subsample set and return this set.
405 
406         For efficiency, we need to subsample the training set to compute scores
407         with scorers.
408         """
409         subsample_size = 10000
410         if X_binned_train.shape[0] > subsample_size:
411             indices = np.arange(X_binned_train.shape[0])
412             stratify = y_train if is_classifier(self) else None
413             indices = resample(indices, n_samples=subsample_size,
414                                replace=False, random_state=seed,
415                                stratify=stratify)
416             X_binned_small_train = X_binned_train[indices]
417             y_small_train = y_train[indices]
418             X_binned_small_train = np.ascontiguousarray(X_binned_small_train)
419             return X_binned_small_train, y_small_train
420         else:
421             return X_binned_train, y_train
422 
423     def _check_early_stopping_scorer(self, X_binned_small_train, y_small_train,
424                                      X_binned_val, y_val):
425         """Check if fitting should be early-stopped based on scorer.
426 
427         Scores are computed on validation data or on training data.
428         """
429         self.train_score_.append(
430             self.scorer_(self, X_binned_small_train, y_small_train)
431         )
432 
433         if self._use_validation_data:
434             self.validation_score_.append(
435                 self.scorer_(self, X_binned_val, y_val)
436             )
437             return self._should_stop(self.validation_score_)
438         else:
439             return self._should_stop(self.train_score_)
440 
441     def _check_early_stopping_loss(self,
442                                    raw_predictions,
443                                    y_train,
444                                    raw_predictions_val,
445                                    y_val):
446         """Check if fitting should be early-stopped based on loss.
447 
448         Scores are computed on validation data or on training data.
449         """
450 
451         self.train_score_.append(
452             -self.loss_(y_train, raw_predictions)
453         )
454 
455         if self._use_validation_data:
456             self.validation_score_.append(
457                 -self.loss_(y_val, raw_predictions_val)
458             )
459             return self._should_stop(self.validation_score_)
460         else:
461             return self._should_stop(self.train_score_)
462 
463     def _should_stop(self, scores):
464         """
465         Return True (do early stopping) if the last n scores aren't better
466         than the (n-1)th-to-last score, up to some tolerance.
467         """
468         reference_position = self.n_iter_no_change + 1
469         if len(scores) < reference_position:
470             return False
471 
472         # A higher score is always better. Higher tol means that it will be
473         # harder for subsequent iteration to be considered an improvement upon
474         # the reference score, and therefore it is more likely to early stop
475         # because of the lack of significant improvement.
476         tol = 0 if self.tol is None else self.tol
477         reference_score = scores[-reference_position] + tol
478         recent_scores = scores[-reference_position + 1:]
479         recent_improvements = [score > reference_score
480                                for score in recent_scores]
481         return not any(recent_improvements)
482 
483     def _bin_data(self, X, rng, is_training_data):
484         """Bin data X.
485 
486         If is_training_data, then set the bin_mapper_ attribute.
487         Else, the binned data is converted to a C-contiguous array.
488         """
489 
490         description = 'training' if is_training_data else 'validation'
491         if self.verbose:
492             print("Binning {:.3f} GB of {} data: ".format(
493                 X.nbytes / 1e9, description), end="", flush=True)
494         tic = time()
495         if is_training_data:
496             X_binned = self.bin_mapper_.fit_transform(X)  # F-aligned array
497         else:
498             X_binned = self.bin_mapper_.transform(X)  # F-aligned array
499             # We convert the array to C-contiguous since predicting is faster
500             # with this layout (training is faster on F-arrays though)
501             X_binned = np.ascontiguousarray(X_binned)
502         toc = time()
503         if self.verbose:
504             duration = toc - tic
505             print("{:.3f} s".format(duration))
506 
507         return X_binned
508 
509     def _print_iteration_stats(self, iteration_start_time):
510         """Print info about the current fitting iteration."""
511         log_msg = ''
512 
513         predictors_of_ith_iteration = [
514             predictors_list for predictors_list in self._predictors[-1]
515             if predictors_list
516         ]
517         n_trees = len(predictors_of_ith_iteration)
518         max_depth = max(predictor.get_max_depth()
519                         for predictor in predictors_of_ith_iteration)
520         n_leaves = sum(predictor.get_n_leaf_nodes()
521                        for predictor in predictors_of_ith_iteration)
522 
523         if n_trees == 1:
524             log_msg += ("{} tree, {} leaves, ".format(n_trees, n_leaves))
525         else:
526             log_msg += ("{} trees, {} leaves ".format(n_trees, n_leaves))
527             log_msg += ("({} on avg), ".format(int(n_leaves / n_trees)))
528 
529         log_msg += "max depth = {}, ".format(max_depth)
530 
531         if self.do_early_stopping_:
532             if self.scoring == 'loss':
533                 factor = -1  # score_ arrays contain the negative loss
534                 name = 'loss'
535             else:
536                 factor = 1
537                 name = 'score'
538             log_msg += "train {}: {:.5f}, ".format(name, factor *
539                                                    self.train_score_[-1])
540             if self._use_validation_data:
541                 log_msg += "val {}: {:.5f}, ".format(
542                     name, factor * self.validation_score_[-1])
543 
544         iteration_time = time() - iteration_start_time
545         log_msg += "in {:0.3f}s".format(iteration_time)
546 
547         print(log_msg)
548 
549     def _raw_predict(self, X):
550         """Return the sum of the leaves values over all predictors.
551 
552         Parameters
553         ----------
554         X : array-like, shape=(n_samples, n_features)
555             The input samples.
556 
557         Returns
558         -------
559         raw_predictions : array, shape (n_samples * n_trees_per_iteration,)
560             The raw predicted values.
561         """
562         X = check_array(X, dtype=[X_DTYPE, X_BINNED_DTYPE],
563                         force_all_finite=False)
564         check_is_fitted(self)
565         if X.shape[1] != self.n_features_:
566             raise ValueError(
567                 'X has {} features but this estimator was trained with '
568                 '{} features.'.format(X.shape[1], self.n_features_)
569             )
570         is_binned = getattr(self, '_in_fit', False)
571         n_samples = X.shape[0]
572         raw_predictions = np.zeros(
573             shape=(self.n_trees_per_iteration_, n_samples),
574             dtype=self._baseline_prediction.dtype
575         )
576         raw_predictions += self._baseline_prediction
577         for predictors_of_ith_iteration in self._predictors:
578             for k, predictor in enumerate(predictors_of_ith_iteration):
579                 if is_binned:
580                     predict = partial(
581                         predictor.predict_binned,
582                         missing_values_bin_idx=self.bin_mapper_.missing_values_bin_idx_  # noqa
583                     )
584                 else:
585                     predict = predictor.predict
586                 raw_predictions[k, :] += predict(X)
587 
588         return raw_predictions
589 
590     def _compute_partial_dependence_recursion(self, grid, target_features):
591         """Fast partial dependence computation.
592 
593         Parameters
594         ----------
595         grid : ndarray, shape (n_samples, n_target_features)
596             The grid points on which the partial dependence should be
597             evaluated.
598         target_features : ndarray, shape (n_target_features)
599             The set of target features for which the partial dependence
600             should be evaluated.
601 
602         Returns
603         -------
604         averaged_predictions : ndarray, shape \
605                 (n_trees_per_iteration, n_samples)
606             The value of the partial dependence function on each grid point.
607         """
608         grid = np.asarray(grid, dtype=X_DTYPE, order='C')
609         averaged_predictions = np.zeros(
610             (self.n_trees_per_iteration_, grid.shape[0]), dtype=Y_DTYPE)
611 
612         for predictors_of_ith_iteration in self._predictors:
613             for k, predictor in enumerate(predictors_of_ith_iteration):
614                 predictor.compute_partial_dependence(grid, target_features,
615                                                      averaged_predictions[k])
616         # Note that the learning rate is already accounted for in the leaves
617         # values.
618 
619         return averaged_predictions

638 class HistGradientBoostingRegressor(BaseHistGradientBoosting, RegressorMixin):
639     """Histogram-based Gradient Boosting Regression Tree.
640 
641     This estimator is much faster than
642     :class:`GradientBoostingRegressor<sklearn.ensemble.GradientBoostingRegressor>`
643     for big datasets (n_samples >= 10 000).
644 
645     This estimator has native support for missing values (NaNs). During
646     training, the tree grower learns at each split point whether samples
647     with missing values should go to the left or right child, based on the
648     potential gain. When predicting, samples with missing values are
649     assigned to the left or right child consequently. If no missing values
650     were encountered for a given feature during training, then samples with
651     missing values are mapped to whichever child has the most samples.
652 
653     This implementation is inspired by
654     `LightGBM <https://github.com/Microsoft/LightGBM>`_.
655 
656     .. note::
657 
658       This estimator is still **experimental** for now: the predictions
659       and the API might change without any deprecation cycle. To use it,
660       you need to explicitly import ``enable_hist_gradient_boosting``::
661 
662         >>> # explicitly require this experimental feature
663         >>> from sklearn.experimental import enable_hist_gradient_boosting  # noqa
664         >>> # now you can import normally from ensemble
665         >>> from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingClassifier
666 
667     Read more in the :ref:`User Guide <histogram_based_gradient_boosting>`.
668 
669     Parameters
670     ----------
671     loss : {'least_squares'}, optional (default='least_squares')
672         The loss function to use in the boosting process. Note that the
673         "least squares" loss actually implements an "half least squares loss"
674         to simplify the computation of the gradient.
675     learning_rate : float, optional (default=0.1)
676         The learning rate, also known as *shrinkage*. This is used as a
677         multiplicative factor for the leaves values. Use ``1`` for no
678         shrinkage.
679     max_iter : int, optional (default=100)
680         The maximum number of iterations of the boosting process, i.e. the
681         maximum number of trees.
682     max_leaf_nodes : int or None, optional (default=31)
683         The maximum number of leaves for each tree. Must be strictly greater
684         than 1. If None, there is no maximum limit.
685     max_depth : int or None, optional (default=None)
686         The maximum depth of each tree. The depth of a tree is the number of
687         nodes to go from the root to the deepest leaf. Must be strictly greater
688         than 1. Depth isn't constrained by default.
689     min_samples_leaf : int, optional (default=20)
690         The minimum number of samples per leaf. For small datasets with less
691         than a few hundred samples, it is recommended to lower this value
692         since only very shallow trees would be built.
693     l2_regularization : float, optional (default=0)
694         The L2 regularization parameter. Use ``0`` for no regularization
695         (default).
696     max_bins : int, optional (default=255)
697         The maximum number of bins to use for non-missing values. Before
698         training, each feature of the input array `X` is binned into
699         integer-valued bins, which allows for a much faster training stage.
700         Features with a small number of unique values may use less than
701         ``max_bins`` bins. In addition to the ``max_bins`` bins, one more bin
702         is always reserved for missing values. Must be no larger than 255.
703     warm_start : bool, optional (default=False)
704         When set to ``True``, reuse the solution of the previous call to fit
705         and add more estimators to the ensemble. For results to be valid, the
706         estimator should be re-trained on the same data only.
707         See :term:`the Glossary <warm_start>`.
708     scoring : str or callable or None, optional (default=None)
709         Scoring parameter to use for early stopping. It can be a single
710         string (see :ref:`scoring_parameter`) or a callable (see
711         :ref:`scoring`). If None, the estimator's default scorer is used. If
712         ``scoring='loss'``, early stopping is checked w.r.t the loss value.
713         Only used if ``n_iter_no_change`` is not None.
714     validation_fraction : int or float or None, optional (default=0.1)
715         Proportion (or absolute size) of training data to set aside as
716         validation data for early stopping. If None, early stopping is done on
717         the training data. Only used if ``n_iter_no_change`` is not None.
718     n_iter_no_change : int or None, optional (default=None)
719         Used to determine when to "early stop". The fitting process is
720         stopped when none of the last ``n_iter_no_change`` scores are better
721         than the ``n_iter_no_change - 1`` -th-to-last one, up to some
722         tolerance. If None or 0, no early-stopping is done.
723     tol : float or None, optional (default=1e-7)
724         The absolute tolerance to use when comparing scores during early
725         stopping. The higher the tolerance, the more likely we are to early
726         stop: higher tolerance means that it will be harder for subsequent
727         iterations to be considered an improvement upon the reference score.
728     verbose: int, optional (default=0)
729         The verbosity level. If not zero, print some information about the
730         fitting process.
731     random_state : int, np.random.RandomStateInstance or None, \
732         optional (default=None)
733         Pseudo-random number generator to control the subsampling in the
734         binning process, and the train/validation data split if early stopping
735         is enabled. See :term:`random_state`.
736 
737     Attributes
738     ----------
739     n_iter_ : int
740         The number of iterations as selected by early stopping (if
741         n_iter_no_change is not None). Otherwise it corresponds to max_iter.
742     n_trees_per_iteration_ : int
743         The number of tree that are built at each iteration. For regressors,
744         this is always 1.
745     train_score_ : ndarray, shape (n_iter_ + 1,)
746         The scores at each iteration on the training data. The first entry
747         is the score of the ensemble before the first iteration. Scores are
748         computed according to the ``scoring`` parameter. If ``scoring`` is
749         not 'loss', scores are computed on a subset of at most 10 000
750         samples. Empty if no early stopping.
751     validation_score_ : ndarray, shape (n_iter_ + 1,)
752         The scores at each iteration on the held-out validation data. The
753         first entry is the score of the ensemble before the first iteration.
754         Scores are computed according to the ``scoring`` parameter. Empty if
755         no early stopping or if ``validation_fraction`` is None.
756 
757     Examples
758     --------
759     >>> # To use this experimental feature, we need to explicitly ask for it:
760     >>> from sklearn.experimental import enable_hist_gradient_boosting  # noqa
761     >>> from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor
762     >>> from sklearn.datasets import load_boston
763     >>> X, y = load_boston(return_X_y=True)
764     >>> est = HistGradientBoostingRegressor().fit(X, y)
765     >>> est.score(X, y)
766     0.98...
767     """
768 
769     _VALID_LOSSES = ('least_squares',)
770 
771     def __init__(self, loss='least_squares', learning_rate=0.1,
772                  max_iter=100, max_leaf_nodes=31, max_depth=None,
773                  min_samples_leaf=20, l2_regularization=0., max_bins=255,
774                  warm_start=False, scoring=None, validation_fraction=0.1,
775                  n_iter_no_change=None, tol=1e-7, verbose=0,
776                  random_state=None):
777         super(HistGradientBoostingRegressor, self).__init__(
778             loss=loss, learning_rate=learning_rate, max_iter=max_iter,
779             max_leaf_nodes=max_leaf_nodes, max_depth=max_depth,
780             min_samples_leaf=min_samples_leaf,
781             l2_regularization=l2_regularization, max_bins=max_bins,
782             warm_start=warm_start, scoring=scoring,
783             validation_fraction=validation_fraction,
784             n_iter_no_change=n_iter_no_change, tol=tol, verbose=verbose,
785             random_state=random_state)

214 class ModelFormMetaclass(DeclarativeFieldsMetaclass):
215     def __new__(mcs, name, bases, attrs):
216         base_formfield_callback = None
217         for b in bases:
218             if hasattr(b, 'Meta') and hasattr(b.Meta, 'formfield_callback'):
219                 base_formfield_callback = b.Meta.formfield_callback
220                 break
221 
222         formfield_callback = attrs.pop('formfield_callback', base_formfield_callback)
223 
224         new_class = super().__new__(mcs, name, bases, attrs)
225 
226         if bases == (BaseModelForm,):
227             return new_class
228 
229         opts = new_class._meta = ModelFormOptions(getattr(new_class, 'Meta', None))
230 
231         # We check if a string was passed to `fields` or `exclude`,
232         # which is likely to be a mistake where the user typed ('foo') instead
233         # of ('foo',)
234         for opt in ['fields', 'exclude', 'localized_fields']:
235             value = getattr(opts, opt)
236             if isinstance(value, str) and value != ALL_FIELDS:
237                 msg = ("%(model)s.Meta.%(opt)s cannot be a string. "
238                        "Did you mean to type: ('%(value)s',)?" % {
239                            'model': new_class.__name__,
240                            'opt': opt,
241                            'value': value,
242                        })
243                 raise TypeError(msg)
244 
245         if opts.model:
246             # If a model is defined, extract form fields from it.
247             if opts.fields is None and opts.exclude is None:
248                 raise ImproperlyConfigured(
249                     "Creating a ModelForm without either the 'fields' attribute "
250                     "or the 'exclude' attribute is prohibited; form %s "
251                     "needs updating." % name
252                 )
253 
254             if opts.fields == ALL_FIELDS:
255                 # Sentinel for fields_for_model to indicate "get the list of
256                 # fields from the model"
257                 opts.fields = None
258 
259             fields = fields_for_model(
260                 opts.model, opts.fields, opts.exclude, opts.widgets,
261                 formfield_callback, opts.localized_fields, opts.labels,
262                 opts.help_texts, opts.error_messages, opts.field_classes,
263                 # limit_choices_to will be applied during ModelForm.__init__().
264                 apply_limit_choices_to=False,
265             )
266 
267             # make sure opts.fields doesn't specify an invalid field
268             none_model_fields = {k for k, v in fields.items() if not v}
269             missing_fields = none_model_fields.difference(new_class.declared_fields)
270             if missing_fields:
271                 message = 'Unknown field(s) (%s) specified for %s'
272                 message = message % (', '.join(missing_fields),
273                                      opts.model.__name__)
274                 raise FieldError(message)
275             # Override default model fields with any custom declared ones
276             # (plus, include all the other declared fields).
277             fields.update(new_class.declared_fields)
278         else:
279             fields = new_class.declared_fields
280 
281         new_class.base_fields = fields
282 
283         return new_class

316     def _get_validation_exclusions(self):
317         """
318         For backwards-compatibility, exclude several types of fields from model
319         validation. See tickets #12507, #12521, #12553.
320         """
321         exclude = []
322         # Build up a list of fields that should be excluded from model field
323         # validation and unique checks.
324         for f in self.instance._meta.fields:
325             field = f.name
326             # Exclude fields that aren't on the form. The developer may be
327             # adding these values to the model after form validation.
328             if field not in self.fields:
329                 exclude.append(f.name)
330 
331             # Don't perform model validation on fields that were defined
332             # manually on the form and excluded via the ModelForm's Meta
333             # class. See #12901.
334             elif self._meta.fields and field not in self._meta.fields:
335                 exclude.append(f.name)
336             elif self._meta.exclude and field in self._meta.exclude:
337                 exclude.append(f.name)
338 
339             # Exclude fields that failed form validation. There's no need for
340             # the model fields to validate them as well.
341             elif field in self._errors:
342                 exclude.append(f.name)
343 
344             # Exclude empty fields that are not required by the form, if the
345             # underlying model field is required. This keeps the model field
346             # from raising a required error. Note: don't exclude the field from
347             # validation if the model field allows blanks. If it does, the blank
348             # value may be included in a unique check, so cannot be excluded
349             # from validation.
350             else:
351                 form_field = self.fields[field]
352                 field_value = self.cleaned_data.get(field)
353                 if not f.blank and not form_field.required and field_value in form_field.empty_values:
354                     exclude.append(f.name)

357     def clean(self):

361     def _update_errors(self, errors):
362         # Override any validation error messages defined at the model level
363         # with those defined at the form level.
364         opts = self._meta
365 
366         # Allow the model generated by construct_instance() to raise
367         # ValidationError and have them handled in the same way as others.
368         if hasattr(errors, 'error_dict'):
369             error_dict = errors.error_dict
370         else:
371             error_dict = {NON_FIELD_ERRORS: errors}
372 
373         for field, messages in error_dict.items():
374             if (field == NON_FIELD_ERRORS and opts.error_messages and
375                     NON_FIELD_ERRORS in opts.error_messages):
376                 error_messages = opts.error_messages[NON_FIELD_ERRORS]
377             elif field in self.fields:
378                 error_messages = self.fields[field].error_messages
379             else:
380                 continue
381 
382             for message in messages:
383                 if (isinstance(message, ValidationError) and
384                         message.code in error_messages):
385                     message.message = error_messages[message.code]
386 
387         self.add_error(None, errors)
388 
389     def _post_clean(self):
390         opts = self._meta
391 
392         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
393 
394         # Foreign Keys being used to represent inline relationships
395         # are excluded from basic field value validation. This is for two
396         # reasons: firstly, the value may not be supplied (#12507; the
397         # case of providing new values to the admin); secondly the
398         # object being referred to may not yet fully exist (#12749).
399         # However, these fields *must* be included in uniqueness checks,
400         # so this can't be part of _get_validation_exclusions().
401         for name, field in self.fields.items():
402             if isinstance(field, InlineForeignKeyField):
403                 exclude.append(name)
404 
405         try:
406             self.instance = construct_instance(self, self.instance, opts.fields, opts.exclude)
407         except ValidationError as e:
408             self._update_errors(e)
409 
410         try:
411             self.instance.full_clean(exclude=exclude, validate_unique=False)
412         except ValidationError as e:
413             self._update_errors(e)
414 
415         # Validate uniqueness if needed.
416         if self._validate_unique:
417             self.validate_unique()
418 
419     def validate_unique(self):
420         """
421         Call the instance's validate_unique() method and update the form's
422         validation errors if any were raised.
423         """
424         exclude = self._get_validation_exclusions()
425         try:
426             self.instance.validate_unique(exclude=exclude)
427         except ValidationError as e:
428             self._update_errors(e)
429 
430     def _save_m2m(self):
431         """
432         Save the many-to-many fields and generic relations for this form.
433         """
434         cleaned_data = self.cleaned_data
435         exclude = self._meta.exclude
436         fields = self._meta.fields
437         opts = self.instance._meta
438         # Note that for historical reasons we want to include also
439         # private_fields here. (GenericRelation was previously a fake
440         # m2m field).
441         for f in chain(opts.many_to_many, opts.private_fields):
442             if not hasattr(f, 'save_form_data'):
443                 continue
444             if fields and f.name not in fields:
445                 continue
446             if exclude and f.name in exclude:
447                 continue
448             if f.name in cleaned_data:
449                 f.save_form_data(self.instance, cleaned_data[f.name])
450 
451     def save(self, commit=True):
452         """
453         Save this form's self.instance object if commit=True. Otherwise, add
454         a save_m2m() method to the form which can be called after the instance
455         is saved manually at a later time. Return the model instance.
456         """
457         if self.errors:
458             raise ValueError(
459                 "The %s could not be %s because the data didn't validate." % (
460                     self.instance._meta.object_name,
461                     'created' if self.instance._state.adding else 'changed',
462                 )
463             )
464         if commit:
465             # If committing, save the instance and the m2m data immediately.
466             self.instance.save()
467             self._save_m2m()
468         else:
469             # If not committing, add a method to the form to allow deferred
470             # saving of m2m data.
471             self.save_m2m = self._save_m2m
472         return self.instance
473 
474     save.alters_data = True

481 def modelform_factory(model, form=ModelForm, fields=None, exclude=None,
482                       formfield_callback=None, widgets=None, localized_fields=None,
483                       labels=None, help_texts=None, error_messages=None,
484                       field_classes=None):
485     """
486     Return a ModelForm containing form fields for the given model. You can
487     optionally pass a `form` argument to use as a starting point for
488     constructing the ModelForm.
489 
490     ``fields`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, include only
491     the named fields in the returned fields. If omitted or '__all__', use all
492     fields.
493 
494     ``exclude`` is an optional list of field names. If provided, exclude the
495     named fields from the returned fields, even if they are listed in the
496     ``fields`` argument.
497 
498     ``widgets`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a widget.
499 
500     ``localized_fields`` is a list of names of fields which should be localized.
501 
502     ``formfield_callback`` is a callable that takes a model field and returns
503     a form field.
504 
505     ``labels`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a label.
506 
507     ``help_texts`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a help text.
508 
509     ``error_messages`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a
510     dictionary of error messages.
511 
512     ``field_classes`` is a dictionary of model field names mapped to a form
513     field class.
514     """
515     # Create the inner Meta class. FIXME: ideally, we should be able to
516     # construct a ModelForm without creating and passing in a temporary
517     # inner class.
518 
519     # Build up a list of attributes that the Meta object will have.
520     attrs = {'model': model}
521     if fields is not None:
522         attrs['fields'] = fields
523     if exclude is not None:
524         attrs['exclude'] = exclude
525     if widgets is not None:
526         attrs['widgets'] = widgets
527     if localized_fields is not None:
528         attrs['localized_fields'] = localized_fields
529     if labels is not None:
530         attrs['labels'] = labels
531     if help_texts is not None:
532         attrs['help_texts'] = help_texts
533     if error_messages is not None:
534         attrs['error_messages'] = error_messages
535     if field_classes is not None:
536         attrs['field_classes'] = field_classes
537 
538     # If parent form class already has an inner Meta, the Meta we're
539     # creating needs to inherit from the parent's inner meta.
540     bases = (form.Meta,) if hasattr(form, 'Meta') else ()
541     Meta = type('Meta', bases, attrs)
542     if formfield_callback:
543         Meta.formfield_callback = staticmethod(formfield_callback)
544     # Give this new form class a reasonable name.
545     class_name = model.__name__ + 'Form'
546 
547     # Class attributes for the new form class.
548     form_class_attrs = {
549         'Meta': Meta,
550         'formfield_callback': formfield_callback
551     }
552 
553     if (getattr(Meta, 'fields', None) is None and
554             getattr(Meta, 'exclude', None) is None):
555         raise ImproperlyConfigured(
556             "Calling modelform_factory without defining 'fields' or "
557             "'exclude' explicitly is prohibited."
558         )
559 
560     # Instantiate type(form) in order to use the same metaclass as form.
561     return type(form)(class_name, (form,), form_class_attrs)

686     def validate_unique(self):
687         # Collect unique_checks and date_checks to run from all the forms.
688         all_unique_checks = set()
689         all_date_checks = set()
690         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
691         valid_forms = [form for form in self.forms if form.is_valid() and form not in forms_to_delete]
692         for form in valid_forms:
693             exclude = form._get_validation_exclusions()
694             unique_checks, date_checks = form.instance._get_unique_checks(exclude=exclude)
695             all_unique_checks.update(unique_checks)
696             all_date_checks.update(date_checks)
697 
698         errors = []
699         # Do each of the unique checks (unique and unique_together)
700         for uclass, unique_check in all_unique_checks:
701             seen_data = set()
702             for form in valid_forms:
703                 # Get the data for the set of fields that must be unique among the forms.
704                 row_data = (
705                     field if field in self.unique_fields else form.cleaned_data[field]
706                     for field in unique_check if field in form.cleaned_data
707                 )
708                 # Reduce Model instances to their primary key values
709                 row_data = tuple(
710                     d._get_pk_val() if hasattr(d, '_get_pk_val')
711                     # Prevent "unhashable type: list" errors later on.
712                     else tuple(d) if isinstance(d, list)
713                     else d for d in row_data
714                 )
715                 if row_data and None not in row_data:
716                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
717                     if row_data in seen_data:
718                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
719                         # the form as invalid
720                         errors.append(self.get_unique_error_message(unique_check))
721                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class([self.get_form_error()])
722                         # remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it was invalid
723                         for field in unique_check:
724                             if field in form.cleaned_data:
725                                 del form.cleaned_data[field]
726                     # mark the data as seen
727                     seen_data.add(row_data)
728         # iterate over each of the date checks now
729         for date_check in all_date_checks:
730             seen_data = set()
731             uclass, lookup, field, unique_for = date_check
732             for form in valid_forms:
733                 # see if we have data for both fields
734                 if (form.cleaned_data and form.cleaned_data[field] is not None and
735                         form.cleaned_data[unique_for] is not None):
736                     # if it's a date lookup we need to get the data for all the fields
737                     if lookup == 'date':
738                         date = form.cleaned_data[unique_for]
739                         date_data = (date.year, date.month, date.day)
740                     # otherwise it's just the attribute on the date/datetime
741                     # object
742                     else:
743                         date_data = (getattr(form.cleaned_data[unique_for], lookup),)
744                     data = (form.cleaned_data[field],) + date_data
745                     # if we've already seen it then we have a uniqueness failure
746                     if data in seen_data:
747                         # poke error messages into the right places and mark
748                         # the form as invalid
749                         errors.append(self.get_date_error_message(date_check))
750                         form._errors[NON_FIELD_ERRORS] = self.error_class([self.get_form_error()])
751                         # remove the data from the cleaned_data dict since it was invalid
752                         del form.cleaned_data[field]
753                     # mark the data as seen
754                     seen_data.add(data)
755 
756         if errors:
757             raise ValidationError(errors)
758 
759     def get_unique_error_message(self, unique_check):
760         if len(unique_check) == 1:
761             return gettext("Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s.") % {
762                 "field": unique_check[0],
763             }
764         else:
765             return gettext("Please correct the duplicate data for %(field)s, which must be unique.") % {
766                 "field": get_text_list(unique_check, _("and")),
767             }
768 
769     def get_date_error_message(self, date_check):
770         return gettext(
771             "Please correct the duplicate data for %(field_name)s "
772             "which must be unique for the %(lookup)s in %(date_field)s."
773         ) % {
774             'field_name': date_check[2],
775             'date_field': date_check[3],
776             'lookup': str(date_check[1]),
777         }

780         return gettext("Please correct the duplicate values below.")

782     def save_existing_objects(self, commit=True):
783         self.changed_objects = []
784         self.deleted_objects = []
785         if not self.initial_forms:
786             return []
787 
788         saved_instances = []
789         forms_to_delete = self.deleted_forms
790         for form in self.initial_forms:
791             obj = form.instance
792             # If the pk is None, it means either:
793             # 1. The object is an unexpected empty model, created by invalid
794             #    POST data such as an object outside the formset's queryset.
795             # 2. The object was already deleted from the database.
796             if obj.pk is None:
797                 continue
798             if form in forms_to_delete:
799                 self.deleted_objects.append(obj)
800                 self.delete_existing(obj, commit=commit)
801             elif form.has_changed():
802                 self.changed_objects.append((obj, form.changed_data))
803                 saved_instances.append(self.save_existing(form, obj, commit=commit))
804                 if not commit:
805                     self.saved_forms.append(form)
806         return saved_instances

808     def save_new_objects(self, commit=True):
809         self.new_objects = []
810         for form in self.extra_forms:
811             if not form.has_changed():
812                 continue
813             # If someone has marked an add form for deletion, don't save the
814             # object.
815             if self.can_delete and self._should_delete_form(form):
816                 continue
817             self.new_objects.append(self.save_new(form, commit=commit))
818             if not commit:
819                 self.saved_forms.append(form)
820         return self.new_objects

822     def add_fields(self, form, index):
823         """Add a hidden field for the object's primary key."""
824         from django.db.models import AutoField, ForeignKey, OneToOneField
825         self._pk_field = pk = self.model._meta.pk
826         # If a pk isn't editable, then it won't be on the form, so we need to
827         # add it here so we can tell which object is which when we get the
828         # data back. Generally, pk.editable should be false, but for some
829         # reason, auto_created pk fields and AutoField's editable attribute is
830         # True, so check for that as well.
831 
832         def pk_is_not_editable(pk):
833             return (
834                 (not pk.editable) or (pk.auto_created or isinstance(pk, AutoField)) or (
835                     pk.remote_field and pk.remote_field.parent_link and
836                     pk_is_not_editable(pk.remote_field.model._meta.pk)
837                 )
838             )
839         if pk_is_not_editable(pk) or pk.name not in form.fields:
840             if form.is_bound:
841                 # If we're adding the related instance, ignore its primary key

1366         also have their label on the bottom and that have the same
1367         bottom-most subplot row.  If the label is on the top,
1368         it is aligned with labels on Axes with the same top-most row.

1371         ----------

1380         matplotlib.figure.Figure.align_labels

1385         their `.SubplotSpec` positions correspond to figure positions.

1387         Examples
1388         --------

1390 
1391             fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 2)

1395             axs[1].set_xlabel('XLabel 1')

1398         if axs is None:

1403             rowspan = ax.get_subplotspec().rowspan
1404             pos = ax.xaxis.get_label_position()  # top or bottom
1405             # Search through other axes for label positions that are same as
1406             # this one and that share the appropriate row number.

1410             for axc in axs:

1412                     rowspanc = axc.get_subplotspec().rowspan
1413                     if (pos == 'top' and rowspan.start == rowspanc.start or

1550         Add a set of subfigures to this figure or subfigure.

1552         A subfigure has the same artist methods as a figure, and is logically
1553         the same as a figure, but cannot print itself.

1580             Defines the relative heights of the rows. Each row gets a
1581             relative height of ``height_ratios[i] / sum(height_ratios)``.

1730         their `.Bbox` in pixels.

1733         in the bbox.

1736         ----------

1739             ``fig.canvas.get_renderer()``)

1743             ``None`` (default), then all artist children of each Axes are
1744             included in the tight bounding box.

1747         -------
1748         `.BboxBase`
1749             containing the bounding box (in figure inches).
1750         """

1752         if renderer is None:
1753             renderer = self.figure._get_renderer()
1754 
1755         bb = []
1756         if bbox_extra_artists is None:
1757             artists = self.get_default_bbox_extra_artists()
1758         else:
1759             artists = bbox_extra_artists
1760 
1761         for a in artists:
1762             bbox = a.get_tightbbox(renderer)
1763             if bbox is not None:
1764                 bb.append(bbox)
1765 
1766         for ax in self.axes:
1767             if ax.get_visible():
1768                 # some axes don't take the bbox_extra_artists kwarg so we
1769                 # need this conditional....
1770                 try:
1771                     bbox = ax.get_tightbbox(
1772                         renderer, bbox_extra_artists=bbox_extra_artists)
1773                 except TypeError:
1774                     bbox = ax.get_tightbbox(renderer)
1775                 bb.append(bbox)

1777               if (np.isfinite(b.width) and np.isfinite(b.height)
1778                   and (b.width != 0 or b.height != 0))]

1992         def _identify_keys_and_nested(mosaic):

2010                 for k, v in enumerate(row):
